items.description: A vast imperial palace complex in central Beijing, consisting of over 980 buildings with golden roofs, red walls, and large courtyards. It houses an extensive collection of Ming and Qing dynasty art, ceramics, and court objects.
items.history: Constructed from 1406 to 1420 during the Ming dynasty, it served as the imperial palace for 24 emperors until 1912. Opened to the public in 1925, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Timed tickets; closed Mondays; expect crowds at holidays.

items.description: The most visited and best-preserved section of the Great Wall, located northwest of Beijing. It features restored watchtowers, steep ramparts, and cable car access.
items.history: Originally built during the Ming dynasty (1368–1644) as a strategic military defense. Opened to tourists in 1957, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Wear layers; sections are steep—comfortable shoes essential.

items.description: A less crowded but equally scenic section of the Great Wall, known for its lush forest surroundings, restored guard towers, and both cable car and toboggan descent options.
items.history: First built in the mid-6th century during the Northern Qi dynasty and later reinforced under the Ming dynasty. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Weekday mornings are quieter; check weather for fog or wind closures.

items.description: A large imperial garden and lake complex in northwestern Beijing, featuring Long Corridor, Marble Boat, Longevity Hill, and Kunming Lake. Popular for boating and walking.
items.history: First built in 1750 during the Qing dynasty and rebuilt after destruction in 1860 and 1900. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Boat rides are popular; allow half a day to walk the full park.

items.description: An imperial sacrificial complex with three famous structures: Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests, Imperial Vault of Heaven, and Circular Mound Altar. Now a public park with morning exercises.
items.history: Built in 1420 during the Ming dynasty for annual prayer ceremonies. Opened as a public park in 1918. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Go early for photos; park is large—plan walking route.

items.description: A sprawling necropolis of 13 Ming dynasty emperors, located in a valley northwest of Beijing. The Sacred Way and Changling tomb are the most visited.
items.history: Built between 1409 and 1644, it was closed to the public until the 20th century. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Combine with Great Wall day trips; shuttle distances between tombs.

items.description: A large urban park in northern Beijing, centered on the Bird’s Nest (National Stadium) and Water Cube. Features wide plazas, walking paths, and light shows at night.
items.history: Built for the 2008 Summer Olympics and reused for the 2022 Winter Olympics. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Evening lighting is popular; interior tours vary by season.

items.description: A well-preserved Qing dynasty princely residence with grand halls, a rock garden, and a large pond. Known for its “luck character” rock and painted corridors.
items.history: Built in the late 18th century for Heshen, later given to Prince Gong in the 1850s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Limited daily tickets—arrive early on peak days.

items.description: A hillside park in western Beijing famous for autumn red leaves, the Glazed Pagoda, and the “Double-Clear” spring. Includes a cable car to the summit.
items.history: Originally part of imperial gardens in the Jin dynasty; rebuilt during the Qing. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Autumn weekends are packed; cable car can reduce climbing.

items.description: A central Beijing imperial garden centered on Taiye Lake, with Qionghua Island, a white Tibetan-style dagoba, lakeside pavilions, and tree-lined walks. Boating in season.
items.history: Landscaped from the Liao–Jin period onward; opened as a public park in 1925. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Combine with nearby Shichahai walks; winter ice when conditions allow.

items.description: A park and museum preserving foundations, lakes, and marble remains of a vast Qing garden-palace complex. Interpretive displays explain the former layout.
items.history: Expanded under Qianlong; severely damaged in 1860 during the Second Opium War. Preserved as a ruins park. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Museum exhibits explain history; large site—wear comfortable shoes.

items.description: A working Tibetan Buddhist monastery in northeastern Beijing, combining prince’s-palace layout with temple halls, incense courtyards, and a large Maitreya statue.
items.history: Built as a prince’s residence in the late Kangxi period, converted into a lamasery in 1744. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: No photos in some halls; respect clockwise circulation.

items.description: The former Imperial College, adjacent to the Confucius Temple, featuring stone stelae, cypress courtyards, and lecture halls. Displays cover state Confucian education.
items.history: Dates to the Yuan capital Dadu; present structures reflect Ming–Qing rebuilding. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Often combined with Confucius Temple ticket; weekdays quieter.

items.description: A north–south hutong lane lined with siheyuan courtyards, small shops, and snack stalls, intersected by east–west side alleys in a historic grid pattern.
items.history: Preserves a Yuan-era street grid; modern renovation turned many units into retail and cafés. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Evenings and holidays are crowded; explore side lanes for calmer lanes.

items.description: Three linked lakes fringed by hutongs, bars, and tea houses. Walking and cycling routes circle the water; winter ice sports when ice thickness permits.
items.history: Part of the Yuan capital water system; surrounding hutong fabric grew dense in the Ming–Qing period. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Ice sports in winter when frozen; bar street can be noisy late.

items.description: A large licensed theme-park resort in Tongzhou, featuring themed lands including The Wizarding World of Harry Potter, rides, shows, and a CityWalk retail zone.
items.history: Opened to the public in September 2021 after construction announced in the 2010s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Use official app for queues; peak days require full-day planning.

items.description: A vast paved civic square south of the Forbidden City, framed by Tiananmen Gate to the north, the Great Hall of the People and the National Museum on east–west flanks, and the Monument to the People’s Heroes and Mausoleum of Mao Zedong along the central axis. It is the usual venue for state ceremonies, flag-raising, and large public gatherings subject to security screening.
items.history: The Ming–Qing city wall and imperial thoroughfare once stood here; the modern square was enlarged in the 1950s–60s to its present dimensions. It has been the setting for major political and ceremonial events in the People’s Republic. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Security checks at entries; national holidays extremely crowded; valid ID may be required.

items.description: A national museum on the east side of Tiananmen Square, with large permanent galleries of ancient Chinese archaeology and art plus rotating modern-history and special exhibitions. The building offers extensive floor space, conservation labs, and auditorium functions; entry is typically free with timed reservation.
items.history: The institution was formed by merging the former National Museum of Chinese History and the Museum of the Chinese Revolution; the present east–west building on the square opened in 2011. It serves as one of China’s principal national museums for history and art on the central axis. It is not a UNESCO site.
items.tips: Free entry with reservation; closed Mondays; allow several hours for major exhibitions.

provinces.description: Beijing is the capital of China, a world-famous ancient capital and modern international metropolis with over 3,000 years of history.
provinces.history: It has served as a capital for more than 860 years. It became the capital of the People's Republic of China in 1949 and is a political, cultural, and international exchange center.
provinces.cuisine: Peking Duck, Zhajiangmian, Douzhi, Tanghulu, Lvdagun

items.description: A 120-meter-tall ferris wheel built over the Yongle Bridge on the Haihe River, offering panoramic night views of Tianjin's skyline. Each cabin holds up to 8 people.
items.history: Opened in 2008 as a landmark for the city's modernization. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Ride tickets sell out—book ahead; best photos at blue hour.

items.nameEn: Five Great Avenues Cultural Tourist Area
items.description: A historic district of over 2,000 restored early-20th-century villas in various European architectural styles. Best explored by bicycle or horse-drawn carriage.
items.history: Developed as a foreign concession area in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Walking or bike share; many buildings are exterior views only.

items.description: A pedestrianized street lined with Qing-style buildings selling traditional crafts, calligraphy, snacks, and the famous Yangliuqing New Year paintings.
items.history: Reconstructed in the 1980s to resemble a late-Qing commercial street. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Very crowded on holidays; watch for pickpockets in crowds.

items.description: A mountainous area east of Beijing known as "the first mountain east of Beijing," featuring ancient temples, rock formations, and a cable car to the summit.
items.history: Developed as a scenic area in the 1980s; historically a retreat for Buddhist monks since the Tang dynasty. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Spring and autumn best; cableways shorten climbs.

items.description: A pedestrian-friendly district of restored early-20th-century Italian-style buildings, now housing restaurants, cafés, and boutiques.
items.history: Originally the Italian concession (1902–1945); restored in the 2000s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Evening dining scene; pedestrian zone can be busy.

items.description: A riverside promenade along the Haihe River, featuring multiple historic bridges, night lights, and boat cruises. Connects several downtown landmarks.
items.history: Developed as a tourist walkway in the early 2000s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Evening lights along the river; boat cruises available seasonally.

items.description: A theme park centered on the decommissioned Soviet aircraft carrier Kiev, allowing visitors to explore the deck, hangar, and missile systems.
items.history: Opened in 2006 after the carrier was purchased from Russia in 2000. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Allow half a day; windy on deck—dress accordingly.

items.description: A large urban park in southern Tianjin featuring two lakes, islands, a Ferris wheel, and recreational boating. Popular for weekend family outings.
items.history: Originally built in 1951 and expanded several times. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Cherry blossom season draws crowds; pedal boats popular.

items.description: A steep and scenic section of the Great Wall east of Beijing, known for its unique "water pass" where the wall meets a river, and well-preserved watchtowers.
items.history: Originally built during the Northern Qi dynasty and reinforced under the Ming. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Combine with Panshan trips; wear sturdy shoes.

items.description: An ancient Buddhist temple featuring one of China's oldest surviving wooden structures — the Guanyin Pavilion, which houses a 16-meter-tall clay sculpture of Guanyin.
items.history: First built in 636 during the Tang dynasty; the main hall dates to 984 (Liao dynasty). It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Small site—pair with nearby ancient streets.

items.description: A French-style villa whose exterior and interior walls are covered with millions of ancient porcelain fragments, vases, and bowls.
items.history: Built as a private museum in the 2000s by collector Zhang Lianzhi. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Admission fee; photography rules apply inside.

provinces.description: Tianjin is a municipality directly under the Central Government, a major port city and economic center in northern China.
provinces.history: Founded in the Ming Dynasty, it is the only Chinese ancient city with a clear recorded founding date. It was one of China's earliest open coastal cities after 1860.
provinces.cuisine: Goubuli Baozi, Jianbing Guozhi, Shibajie Mahua, Erduoyan Zhagao

items.description: A famous waterfront promenade on the west bank of the Huangpu River, lined with 52 historic buildings in Art Deco, Gothic, and Neoclassical styles, facing the futuristic Pudong skyline.
items.history: Developed as a foreign concession area after the 1842 Treaty of Nanking. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Sunrise and night lights are iconic; weekends very crowded.

items.description: A classical Chinese garden in the Old City, featuring rockeries, ponds, pavilions, and the famous Exquisite Jade Rock. Now surrounded by the bustling Yuyuan Bazaar.
items.history: First built in 1559 during the Ming dynasty by Pan Yunduan. Restored and opened to the public in 1961. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Go early to avoid tour groups; tight paths when crowded.

items.description: A large theme park resort in Pudong, featuring six themed lands, the tallest Disney castle (Enchanted Storybook Castle), and unique attractions like Tron Lightcycle Power Run.
items.history: Opened on June 16, 2016, as the first Disney resort in mainland China. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Use official app for queues; avoid major holidays if possible.

items.description: A 468-meter-tall tower in Pudong with 11 spheres of varying sizes. Features observation decks, a revolving restaurant, and a glass-bottomed skywalk.
items.history: Completed in 1995 as Shanghai's first modern skyscraper and a symbol of Pudong's development. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Sunset slots popular—book tickets; can be hazy.

items.description: A canal town on the outskirts of Shanghai, featuring stone bridges, Ming- and Qing-era houses, narrow alleys, and boat rides along the water.
items.history: Settled over 1,700 years ago; became a commercial center during the Ming and Qing dynasties. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Weekends crowded; arrive morning for calmer lanes.

items.description: A warren of restored lane houses (shikumen) in the French Concession, now filled with art studios, boutiques, cafés, and street art.
items.history: Originally a residential area from the 1930s; redeveloped into an arts district in the early 2000s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Narrow alleys—difficult with strollers; evenings lively.

items.description: A large alluvial island at the mouth of the Yangtze River, featuring Dongtan Wetland, bird watching, cycling trails, and organic farms.
items.history: Formed by sediment deposition over centuries; developed as an eco-tourism destination since the 2000s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Ferry or bridge access—plan day-trip timing.

items.description: A 1.2-km-long pedestrian shopping street in central Shanghai, lined with department stores, brand shops, snack stalls, and historic buildings.
items.history: First opened as a commercial street in the 19th century; pedestrianized in 1999. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Evening crowds peak; watch belongings in dense areas.

items.description: A Buddhist temple with golden roofs and a silver pagoda, located on busy Nanjing West Road. Features a 3-ton jade Buddha and a large bronze bell.
items.history: First built in 247 CE during the Three Kingdoms period; rebuilt in its current form in the 20th century. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Metro access; short visit unless attending services.

items.description: A iconic wedge-shaped apartment building in the French Concession, with a ship-like prow at the intersection of five streets.
items.history: Designed by Hungarian architect László Hudec and completed in 1924. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Street photography spot—respect residents' privacy.

items.description: A restored residential enclave of 51 early-20th-century garden villas in the French Concession, now housing boutiques, restaurants, and a bookshop.
items.history: Originally built in the 1920s–30s; restored and reopened in the 2010s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Upscale area; outdoor events seasonal.

items.description: A waterfront promenade on the east bank of the Huangpu River in Pudong, offering unobstructed views of the Bund and walking/cycling paths.
items.history: Developed in the late 1990s as part of the Lujiazui financial district. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Evening strolls best; connects to Lujiazui sights.

items.description: An archaeological park featuring partially submerged museum buildings shaped like ancient pottery shards, displaying artifacts from the Songze and Guangfulin cultures.
items.history: Excavations began in the 1950s; the site dates back 4,000–5,000 years. The park opened in 2018. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Large park—half-day visit; combine with Sheshan if time allows.

provinces.description: Shanghai is China's economic, financial, trade and shipping center, an international metropolis.
provinces.history: It developed rapidly after opening as a port in 1843. It is a fusion city of Chinese and Western cultures with important modern historical significance.
provinces.cuisine: Xiaolongbao, Shengjianbao, Shanghai Hairy Crab, Scallion Oil Noodles

items.description: A multi-level stilt-house complex on the Jialing River, featuring traditional Bayu architecture, night lights, snack streets, and views of the Qiansimen Bridge.
items.history: Rebuilt in 2006 on the site of a former cliff-side settlement. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Evenings extremely crowded; arrive early for photos.

items.nameEn: Three Gorges of the Yangtze River
items.description: A 193-km stretch of the Yangtze River through three dramatic gorges — Qutang, Wu, and Xiling — best experienced by cruise ship.
items.history: Formed by millions of years of erosion; partially flooded by the Three Gorges Dam (completed 2012). It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Cruise schedules vary by season; book upstream/downstream legs in advance.

items.description: A UNESCO-listed South China Karst landscape in Wulong: massive sinkholes, natural stone bridges (including the Three Natural Bridges — Tianlong, Qinglong, and Heilong), Furong Cave, and gorges over 100 meters high.
items.history: Inscribed in 2007 as part of the South China Karst World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Rain makes paths slippery; shuttle buses from visitor center.

items.description: A high-altitude grassland resort in Wulong, known as the "Switzerland of Chongqing," featuring rolling pastures, horse riding, and winter skiing.
items.history: Developed as a tourist resort in the 2000s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Cooler than downtown—bring jacket; fog common.

items.description: A series of over 50,000 Buddhist, Taoist, and Confucian rock carvings and statues spread across 75 cliff sites in Dazu District.
items.history: Carved from the 7th to 13th centuries, mainly during the Tang and Song dynasties. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Baodingshan and Beishan are main clusters—plan transport between sites.

items.description: A historic river town on the Jialing River, featuring stone-paved streets, traditional courtyard houses, tea houses, and Sichuan snack stalls.
items.history: A former commercial port during the Ming and Qing dynasties; restored as a tourist street in the 2000s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Weekends packed; try early weekday visit.

items.description: A busy shopping and commercial hub in central Chongqing, centered on the War of Resistance Monument (Jiefangbei).
items.history: Originally built as a spiritual fortress in 1941; pedestrianized in 1997. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Shopping and metro hub; very dense at night.

items.description: A unique light rail station where the train passes directly through the 6th to 8th floors of a residential building. A popular photo spot.
items.history: Opened in 2004 as part of Chongqing's Rail Transit Line 2. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Viewing platform often crowded; mind traffic below.

items.description: A 1.1-km-long aerial tramway crossing the Yangtze River, offering panoramic views of the city and river.
items.history: Opened in 1987 as a commuter crossing; became a tourist attraction in the 2010s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Queues long at rush hour; avoid if afraid of heights.

items.description: A hilltop fortress overlooking the Qutang Gorge, famous for its association with the Three Kingdoms and the poet Li Bai.
items.history: Originally built during the Eastern Han dynasty (25–220 CE); later a Tang dynasty poem site. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Often visited on Three Gorges cruises; many steps.

items.description: The shortest and narrowest of the Three Gorges, with dramatic cliffs at Kui Gate; best seen from cruise ships or viewpoints near Baidicheng.
items.history: Formed by Yangtze erosion; water levels rose after the Three Gorges Dam. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Best seen from cruise deck; weather affects visibility.

items.description: A deep gorge and forest park in Wansheng District, featuring a 13-km walking trail along a river, waterfalls, and a hanging plank walkway.
items.history: Developed as a national park in the early 2000s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Slippery after rain; shuttle from gate.

items.description: A karst mountain in southern Chongqing, known for its "pillar-shaped peaks," Buddhist temples, and a cable car to the summit.
items.history: Designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014 as part of the South China Karst.
items.tips: Cableways may close in wind; check alerts.

items.description: A well-preserved cliff-side town on the Wu River, featuring stone-paved alleys, stilted houses, and a historic salt dock.
items.history: Originally built over 1,700 years ago; relocated and rebuilt in the 2000s due to dam construction. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Remote—overnight stay common; river level affects docks.

provinces.description: Chongqing is a municipality directly under the Central Government, known as 'Mountain City' and 'Fog City', the economic center of the upper Yangtze River.
provinces.history: It was the ancient State of Ba. It served as the wartime capital during the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. It has unique mountain city scenery.
provinces.cuisine: Chongqing Hot Pot, Xiaomian, Maoxuewang, Wanzhou Grilled Fish

items.nameCn: 承德避暑山庄及周围寺庙
items.nameEn: Chengde Mountain Resort and Outlying Temples
items.description: A vast imperial summer retreat complex with lakes, forests, and pavilions, surrounded by eight Tibetan- and Han-style temples.
items.history: Built between 1703 and 1792 during the Qing dynasty for summer court sessions. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Allow full day; temple zones require separate tickets.

items.description: Eight Tibetan- and Han-style Buddhist temples outside the resort, built by Qing emperors for state rituals and to receive Mongol and Tibetan envoys.
items.history: Built in the 18th century as part of the Chengde palace-temple ensemble. Listed with the resort as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Combine with resort ticket bundles; hilly walking.

items.description: A coastal resort town on the Bohai Sea, known for its sandy beaches, pine forests, and mild summer climate. Popular for swimming and sunbathing.
items.history: Developed as a foreign beach resort in the late 19th century; later a Chinese leadership retreat. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: July–August peak season; check swim flags.

items.description: A fortified pass where the Great Wall meets the sea, known as the "First Pass Under Heaven." Features a restored gate tower and museum.
items.history: Originally built in 1381 during the Ming dynasty. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Windy coast—layer clothing; combine with Laolongtou.

items.description: A karst mountain with white marble peaks, glass-bottomed skywalks, and a 2.5-km-long cliff-side plank road in Laiyuan County.
items.history: Developed as a scenic area in the 2000s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Not for severe vertigo; weather can close glass decks.

items.description: A sprawling necropolis of 5 Qing emperors (including Kangxi and Qianlong), 15 empresses, and 136 other royal figures, located in Zunhua.
items.history: Built between 1661 and 1908. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: UNESCO site; spread out—need vehicle between tombs.

items.description: A necropolis of 4 Qing emperors (including Yongzheng and Guangxu) and their consorts, located in Yi County.
items.history: Built between 1730 and 1915. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Less visited than Eastern—quieter photography.

items.description: A large natural area in Laishui County, featuring karst gorges, waterfalls, caves, and the Baili Gorge (Hundred-Mile Gorge).
items.history: Developed as a national park in the 1980s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Summer rafting season; winter activities limited.

items.description: A large shallow lake with over 100 small islets, reed marshes, and lotus flowers. Known for boat tours and duck egg snacks.
items.history: Formed naturally; became a tourist destination in the 1990s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Lotus bloom mid-summer; negotiate boat prices clearly.

items.description: A mountain famous for the "Five Heroes of Langya Mountain," who jumped off its cliff during the Second Sino-Japanese War. Features a memorial tower.
items.history: Site of the 1941 battle; a memorial was built in 1958. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Steep stairs; patriotic exhibits at summit.

items.description: A well-preserved section of the Great Wall in Luanping County, known for its dense watchtowers, steep slopes, and popular sunrise photography spots.
items.history: First built during the Northern Qi dynasty; reinforced under the Ming. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Sunrise photography popular—carry water.

items.description: A large artificial forest park in northern Hebei, known for its larch and birch forests, grasslands, and autumn colors.
items.history: Planted from 1962 onward as a reforestation project. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Cold nights even in summer; autumn colors stunning.

items.description: A large shallow lake and wetland in southern Hebei, known for migratory birds (cranes, swans), lotus flowers, and walking trails.
items.history: Designated as a national nature reserve in 2000. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Bird migration seasons best; bring binoculars.

provinces.description: Hebei is located in the North China Plain, surrounding Beijing and Tianjin, with rich historical and cultural heritage.
provinces.history: It was the territory of Yan, Zhao and Zhongshan States in the Spring and Autumn and Warring States Periods. It has many world-famous historical sites.
provinces.cuisine: Donkey Meat Sandwich, Jinfeng Braised Chicken, Zhengding Eight Bowls

items.description: A well-preserved Ming- and Qing-era walled city with traditional courtyard houses, banks, shops, and a 6-km city wall.
items.history: Founded in the 14th century; remained largely unchanged after the 19th century. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: UNESCO site—stay overnight for lantern evenings.

items.description: A series of 252 caves and over 51,000 Buddhist stone statues carved into a sandstone cliff west of Datong.
items.history: Carved between 460 and 525 CE during the Northern Wei dynasty. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Crowded midday; caves numbered 1–20 along cliff.

items.description: A sacred Buddhist mountain with over 50 temples, pagodas, and monasteries scattered across five flat peaks. A pilgrimage site for Chinese Buddhists.
items.history: Designated as a Buddhist site from the 1st century CE; flourished during the Tang dynasty. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Cool summers; altitude and weather change quickly.

items.description: A 50-meter-wide, 20-meter-high waterfall on the Yellow River, where the river narrows dramatically into a "teapot spout." Best viewed from the Shanxi side.
items.history: Formed naturally; a famous landmark for centuries. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Peak flow summer; mist soaks cameras.

items.description: A large Qing-era courtyard complex with 313 rooms, known for its intricate wood carvings, brick carvings, and as the filming location for "Raise the Red Lantern."
items.history: Built between 1756 and the early 20th century by the wealthy Qiao merchant family. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Popular after film fame—go early.

items.description: A massive Ming- and Qing-era courtyard complex with 1,234 rooms, often called the "Forbidden City of Shanxi."
items.history: Built over 300 years by the Wang merchant family. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Allow 2–3 hours; many stairs between courtyards.

items.description: A well-preserved Ming- and Qing-era official's residence and defensive fortress, built by the Chen family, who produced multiple imperial officials.
items.history: Constructed from the 15th to 18th centuries. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Hilly site—comfortable shoes; cultural shows seasonal.

items.description: A Taoist sacred mountain with temples, caves, and a cliff-hanging hotel. Known for its suspension bridges and spring waterfalls.
items.history: Associated with Jie Zitui (7th century BCE); temples date to the Tang and Ming dynasties. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Long scenic bus route inside park.

items.description: A temple complex dedicated to the Tang dynasty founder's mother, featuring the 1,000-year-old "Lady Sculpture Hall" and the "Flying Bridge over Fish Pond."
items.history: First built in the 12th century BCE; present structures mainly from the Northern Qi and Song dynasties. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Morning light best for hall photography.

items.description: A series of 25 Buddhist caves carved into a mountainside southwest of Taiyuan, with many statues now headless due to theft.
items.history: Carved between the 6th and 8th centuries (Eastern Wei to Tang dynasties). It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Shuttle road winding; combine with Jinci.

items.description: A 67-meter-tall, nine-story wooden pagoda, the oldest and tallest all-wooden pagoda in the world, without a single metal nail.
items.history: Built in 1056 during the Liao dynasty. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Interior access limited; admire from plaza.

items.description: A Buddhist, Taoist, and Confucian temple built into a cliff face 75 meters above the ground, supported by wooden beams inserted into the rock.
items.history: First built in 491 CE during the Northern Wei dynasty; rebuilt in the 20th century. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Steep stairs; not for acrophobia.

provinces.description: Shanxi is an important birthplace of Chinese civilization, known as the 'Museum of Ancient Chinese Architecture'.
provinces.history: It was the powerful Jin State in the Spring and Autumn Period. It has three world cultural heritages: Pingyao Ancient City, Yungang Grottoes and Wutai Mountain.
provinces.cuisine: Daoxiao Noodles, Pingyao Beef, Youmian Kaolaolao, Shanxi Aged Vinegar

items.description: A vast, rolling grassland in northeastern Inner Mongolia, known for its "sea of grass," nomadic herders, horseback riding, and summer naadam festivals.
items.history: Traditionally inhabited by Mongol herders for centuries; developed as a tourist destination since the 1990s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Summer best; mosquitos near wetlands; book drivers in advance.

items.addressFull: Ejina Banner, Alxa, Inner Mongolia, China
items.description: A desert forest of ancient poplar (Populus euphratica) trees, turning golden in late October. Famous for its "living for 1,000 years, standing for 1,000 years after death" legend.
items.history: Protected as a nature reserve since 1992. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Peak week is crowded—book lodging months ahead.

items.addressFull: Dalad Banner, Ordos, Inner Mongolia, China
items.description: A desert recreation area in the Kubuqi Desert, known for dunes that "sing" when wind blows or sand slides. Features camel rides, sand sledding, and a desert cable car.
items.history: Developed as a tourist attraction in the 1980s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Sun protection essential; sand gets hot midday.

items.description: A volcanic forest park in northeastern Inner Mongolia, featuring crater lakes, hot springs, wetlands, and autumn larch forests.
items.history: Developed as a national park in the 2000s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Cold nights; autumn foliage spectacular.

items.addressFull: Ejin Horo Banner, Ordos, Inner Mongolia, China
items.description: A memorial complex dedicated to Genghis Khan, featuring three large yurt-shaped halls, a 5-meter-tall statue of the Khan, and ritual offerings.
items.history: Original burial site unknown; the present mausoleum was built in 1954. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Respect ritual areas; windy steppe climate.

items.description: A typical Mongolian grassland in central Inner Mongolia, known for its wide horizons, horse riding, and the annual Naadam Festival (wrestling, horse racing, archery).
items.history: Traditionally inhabited by Mongol herders. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Road distances long—fuel and supplies planning needed.

items.description: A border crossing point between China and Russia, featuring a large Chinese border gate, a 41st boundary marker, and views of the Russian town of Zabaikalsk.
items.history: Established as a border town in the late 19th century; the current gate was built in 2008. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Bring passport if cross-border tours offered; winter very cold.

items.addressFull: Chahar Right Middle Banner, Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, China
items.description: A high-altitude grassland (2,000 meters above sea level) in central Inner Mongolia, dotted with thousands of wind turbines. Known for yellow flowers in summer.
items.history: Traditionally used as summer pasture. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Dress for wind; altitude cooler than Beijing.

items.addressFull: Alxa Right Banner, Inner Mongolia, China
items.description: A desert famous for having the world's tallest stationary sand dunes (some over 500 meters high) and over 100 permanent desert lakes.
items.history: Formed naturally; opened for tourism in the 2000s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: 4WD tours required; carry water; summer heat extreme.

items.addressFull: Hexigten Banner, Chifeng, Inner Mongolia, China
items.description: A grassland in southeastern Inner Mongolia, known as a filming location for historical Chinese TV dramas (e.g., "Kangxi Dynasty") and autumn photography.
items.history: Traditionally a hunting ground for Qing emperors. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Remote roads; join local guides for off-road safety.

provinces.description: Inner Mongolia is the first ethnic autonomous region in China, with vast grasslands and unique nomadic culture.
provinces.history: It was an important activity area for ancient nomadic peoples. It has a long history of ethnic integration and rich natural grassland resources.
provinces.cuisine: Shouba Rou, Roasted Whole Lamb, Milk Tea, Mongolian Hot Pot, Milk Skin

items.description: A 114-building palace complex in central Shenyang, featuring Manchu-style architecture with "five-courtyard" layout, large square, and Dazheng Hall.
items.history: Built between 1625 and 1636 by Nurhaci and Huangtaiji; later expanded under Qianlong. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Allow 2 hours; nearby Zhang's mansion optional.

items.description: A 5.8-km-long underground river cave in Benxi, accessible by boat for 2.5 km. Features stalactites, stalagmites, and a large underground chamber.
items.history: Discovered in 1983 and opened as a tourist attraction in 1994. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Jackets provided—cold inside; queues on holidays.

items.description: A mountainous area with 999 granite peaks, known as the "Treasure Land of Northeast China." Features Buddhist and Taoist temples, and a cable car.
items.history: Developed as a Buddhist site from the Tang dynasty onward. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Weekend crowds; start early.

items.description: A large urban plaza in Dalian, facing the Yellow Sea. Features a 100-year-old monument, a seaside promenade, and a musical fountain.
items.history: Built in 1997 to celebrate the 100th anniversary of Dalian's founding. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Windy; evening light shows seasonal.

items.description: A coastal wetland covered with red Suaeda salsa plants (turn red in autumn), forming a "red carpet" along the Liaohe River delta.
items.history: Protected as a nature reserve since 1992; opened for tourism in the 2000s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Best color window September–October; mind tides.

items.description: A large marine park in Dalian, featuring a polar animal pavilion, coral aquarium, dolphin shows, and a seaside cable car.
items.history: Opened in 1992 and expanded several times. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Family queues long—arrive opening.

items.description: A coastal national park in Dalian with 3–6 km of sandy beaches, limestone rock formations, dinosaur fossils, and a golf course.
items.history: Designated as a national scenic area in 1988. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Coastal wind; combine with light rail from Dalian.

items.description: A mountain in Dandong known for its steep cliffs, hanging plank walkways, and views of the Yalu River and North Korea.
items.history: Developed as a scenic area in the 1980s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Not for faint-hearted; check weather closures.

items.description: A sacred mountain in Jinzhou, known as one of the "Five Sacred Mountains of the Northeast," featuring Taoist temples and ancient pine trees.
items.history: First mentioned in the Zhou dynasty; developed as a pilgrimage site from the Tang dynasty. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Spring pilgrimages busy.

items.description: A large botanical garden in eastern Shenyang, known as the "Backyard of Shenyang," featuring themed gardens, a large lake, and a children's play area.
items.history: Founded in 1959 and expanded in the 1990s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Spring flower events popular; wear walking shoes.

provinces.description: Liaoning is an important old industrial base in China and the birthplace of Manchu culture.
provinces.history: It was the birthplace of the Manchu people. Shenyang Imperial Palace is a world cultural heritage. It has a long industrial and historical heritage.
provinces.cuisine: Guobaorou, Chicken Stewed with Mushrooms, Dalian Seafood, Shenyang Cold Noodles

items.description: A volcanic mountain on the China–North Korea border, featuring Heaven Lake (a crater lake), hot springs, waterfalls, and alpine tundra.
items.history: Designated as a nature reserve in 1960; opened for tourism in the 1980s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Weather closes summit often; permits and buses required.

items.addressFull: Chuanying District, Jilin City, Jilin, China
items.description: A small island on the Songhua River, known for its winter rime frost (thick ice crystals on trees) from December to February.
items.history: Developed as a winter photography destination in the 2000s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Best December–February early morning; extreme cold.

items.description: A restored palace complex that served as the residence of Puyi (last Qing emperor) during the Japanese puppet state of Manchukuo (1932–1945).
items.history: Built in the 1930s; opened as a museum in 1962. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Allow 2–3 hours; audio guides helpful.

items.description: A large urban forest park in Changchun, centered on a crescent-shaped reservoir. Features a golf course, winter skiing, and summer boating.
items.history: Built as a water reservoir in 1934; reforested from the 1950s onward. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Large—rent bikes or use shuttle.

items.description: A large freshwater lake in Songyuan, known for its winter ice fishing festival (December–January) using traditional horse-drawn nets.
items.history: Traditional fishing grounds for centuries; modern tourism started in the 2000s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Winter only for ice fishing tourism—dress heavily.

items.addressFull: Fengman District, Jilin City, Jilin, China
items.description: A large reservoir on the Songhua River, formed by the Fengman Dam. Features boating, fishing, and autumn maple leaf views.
items.history: Dam built by the Japanese in 1937–1942; became a scenic area in the 1980s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Dam area viewpoints; fog mornings.

items.description: A theme park based on Chinese cinema, featuring 3D/4D theaters, stunt shows, and sets from famous Chinese films.
items.history: Opened in 2005 by Changchun Film Studio (China's oldest film studio, founded 1945). It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Family-oriented; seasonal hours.

items.description: A hillside complex featuring a giant bronze sitting Buddha (48 meters high), a Qing dynasty royal temple, and a Dongbei folk culture village.
items.history: Buddhist site since the Tang dynasty; the Buddha statue was completed in 2011. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Respect temple etiquette; cold winters.

items.description: A reconstructed Korean-style village in Yanbian, offering traditional Korean houses, food (kimchi, bibimbap), and cultural performances.
items.history: Built as a tourist attraction in the 2000s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Try seasonal festivals; language mix Korean/Mandarin.

provinces.description: Jilin is located in central Northeast China, famous for Changbai Mountain, rime scenery and Korean ethnic culture.
provinces.history: It is one of the birthplaces of Manchu culture. It has unique natural scenery and multi-cultural integration characteristics.
provinces.cuisine: Yanbian Cold Noodles, Korean Rice Cake, Ginseng Chicken, Korean Barbecue

items.addressFull: Mohe, Da Hinggan Ling, Heilongjiang, China
items.description: A riverside village on the Amur River, China's northernmost settlement. Known for winter temperatures below -40°C, aurora borealis (rare), and the "Midnight Sun" in summer.
items.history: Established as a logging town in the 1960s; developed as a tourism destination in the 1990s. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Winter −40°C possible—extreme cold gear; summer midnight sun.

items.description: A seasonal winter theme park featuring massive ice and snow sculptures, illuminated at night, with ice slides, ice lanterns, and performances.
items.history: First held in 1999; now an annual event from late December to February. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Dress in layers; slippery—cleats help.

items.description: A volcanic landscape with five interconnected lakes formed by lava flows, plus mineral springs, lava caves, and volcanic cones.
items.history: Formed by volcanic eruptions in 1719–1721. It is a UNESCO Global Geopark.
items.tips: Geology trails spread out—need car or tour bus.

items.description: A large volcanic barrier lake in Mudanjiang, formed by lava blocking the Mudan River. Features Diaoshuilou Waterfall (20 meters high) and a 40-km-long lake.
items.history: Formed by volcanic activity about 10,000 years ago. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Summer boating; winter ice road access varies.

items.description: A large wetland in Qiqihar, known as the "hometown of the red-crowned crane," with over 300 cranes in captivity and wild populations.
items.history: Established as a nature reserve in 1979; a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Crane flight times posted—telephoto lens useful.

items.description: A large island park in the Songhua River in Harbin, featuring Russian-style architecture, a polar animal pavilion, and winter snow sculpture exhibitions.
items.history: Developed as a resort in the 1950s; site of the annual Snow Sculpture Art Expo. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Ice festival overlaps Ice World—plan combined tickets.

items.description: A large breeding and viewing facility for Siberian tigers in Harbin, with over 500 tigers in semi-wild enclosures. Visitors take bus tours through the park.
items.history: Founded in 1996 to protect and breed endangered Siberian tigers. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Stay in vehicles on safari route; ethical debates exist.

items.description: A granite rock forest in Yichun, featuring unusually shaped boulders (like a "frog" and "walnut man") surrounded by dense forest.
items.history: Designated as a national geopark in 2008. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Mosquitos in summer; boardwalks icy in winter.

items.description: A vast, sparsely populated boreal forest region in northern Heilongjiang, known for autumn colors, wild berries, and hiking trails.
items.history: Historically inhabited by Oroqen and Evenki reindeer herders; logging reduced after 2000. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Travel with local guides; fire bans strict.

items.description: A riverside square on the Amur River, China's easternmost point. Features a large "East Pole" monument and the first sunrise of China (around 4 AM in summer).
items.history: Built in 2005 to mark the easternmost point of China. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Remote—check border regulations; sunrise tourism popular.

items.description: A 1.5-km-long pedestrian street in Harbin, lined with European-style buildings (Baroque, Byzantine, Art Nouveau) and the famous 1909 Jewish synagogue.
items.history: Built by Russian engineers in 1898; paved with stone blocks in 1924. It is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.bestVisitTime: Year-round; winter for ice festival atmosphere
items.tips: Ice slippery in winter; peak season very crowded; try local ice cream (malatang) along the walk.

provinces.description: Heilongjiang is China's northernmost province, famous for ice-snow culture, forests and wetland resources.
provinces.history: It has a long frontier history. Harbin is known as the 'Ice City'. It has unique Sino-Russian cultural integration characteristics.
provinces.cuisine: Harbin Red Sausage, Demoli Stewed Fish, Dalieba, Madeier Ice Cream

items.description: A group of classical Chinese gardens in Suzhou, famous for exquisite rockeries, peaceful ponds, winding corridors, and delicate landscaping. They represent the highest achievement of private garden art in southern China, integrating architecture, painting, and poetry.
items.history: Suzhou's garden-building tradition began in the 6th century BC and flourished during the Ming and Qing dynasties. The four gardens listed are UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Humble Administrator's Garden was built in the early 16th century; Lingering Garden dates to the Ming Dynasty; Lion Grove Garden is known for its Taihu rocks and was founded in the Yuan Dynasty; Master of the Nets Garden is a compact masterpiece from the Southern Song Dynasty.
items.tips: Reserve timed entry; peak holidays crowded.

items.description: A group of classical Chinese gardens in Suzhou, famous for exquisite rockeries, peaceful ponds, winding corridors, and delicate landscaping. They represent the highest achievement of private garden art in southern China, integrating architecture, painting, and poetry.
items.history: Suzhou's garden-building tradition began in the 6th century BC and flourished during the Ming and Qing dynasties. The four gardens listed are UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Humble Administrator's Garden was built in the early 16th century; Lingering Garden dates to the Ming Dynasty; Lion Grove Garden is known for its Taihu rocks and was founded in the Yuan Dynasty; Master of the Nets Garden is a compact masterpiece from the Southern Song Dynasty.
items.tips: Combine ticket bundles with other gardens if available.

items.description: A group of classical Chinese gardens in Suzhou, famous for exquisite rockeries, peaceful ponds, winding corridors, and delicate landscaping. They represent the highest achievement of private garden art in southern China, integrating architecture, painting, and poetry.
items.history: Suzhou's garden-building tradition began in the 6th century BC and flourished during the Ming and Qing dynasties. The four gardens listed are UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Humble Administrator's Garden was built in the early 16th century; Lingering Garden dates to the Ming Dynasty; Lion Grove Garden is known for its Taihu rocks and was founded in the Yuan Dynasty; Master of the Nets Garden is a compact masterpiece from the Southern Song Dynasty.
items.tips: Tight spaces when busy—mind steps.

items.description: A group of classical Chinese gardens in Suzhou, famous for exquisite rockeries, peaceful ponds, winding corridors, and delicate landscaping. They represent the highest achievement of private garden art in southern China, integrating architecture, painting, and poetry.
items.history: Suzhou's garden-building tradition began in the 6th century BC and flourished during the Ming and Qing dynasties. The four gardens listed are UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Humble Administrator's Garden was built in the early 16th century; Lingering Garden dates to the Ming Dynasty; Lion Grove Garden is known for its Taihu rocks and was founded in the Yuan Dynasty; Master of the Nets Garden is a compact masterpiece from the Southern Song Dynasty.
items.tips: Evening shows sell out—book ahead.

items.description: A grand memorial complex built on the southern slope of Zijin Mountain, featuring traditional Chinese architectural style with symmetrical layout, wide staircases, and solemn memorial halls. It is a major patriotic and cultural landmark in Nanjing.
items.history: Construction began in 1926 and was completed in 1929 to commemorate Dr. Sun Yat-sen, the pioneer of China's democratic revolution. The mausoleum was designed by architect Lü Yanzhi and combines imperial Chinese style with modern monumentality.
items.tips: Free entry; long climb—avoid midday heat.

items.nameEn: Confucius Temple & Qinhuai River Scenic Area
items.description: A historic cultural and commercial zone centered on the Confucius Temple, with riverside streets, traditional architecture, folk performances, and local snacks. It reflects the lively urban culture of ancient Jinling (Nanjing).
items.history: The Confucius Temple was first built in the Song Dynasty. The area prospered as a cultural and entertainment center during the Ming and Qing dynasties. It was restored multiple times after wars and became a famous scenic belt combining history, folk custom, and water scenery.
items.tips: Night boat tours popular; very crowded holidays.

items.description: One of China's most famous water towns, crisscrossed by rivers, with stone bridges, whitewashed houses, and wooden boats. It preserves a well-preserved ancient water-town layout and lifestyle.
items.history: Zhouzhuang's history dates back over 900 years. It boomed during the Ming and Qing dynasties as a trading and shipping hub. It gained worldwide fame after being promoted by artists and writers in the late 20th century.
items.tips: Stay overnight to see dawn without day-trippers.

items.description: A peaceful water town with rivers dividing the town into seven islands, connected by stone bridges. It features well-preserved Ming and Qing residences and a quiet atmosphere.
items.history: Founded over 1,000 years ago, Tongli was a prosperous commercial town in the Ming and Qing dynasties. It avoided major warfare, allowing ancient architecture and water-town structure to remain intact.
items.tips: Ticket covers multiple small gardens inside.

items.description: An ancient water town known for its many ancient stone bridges, simple folk houses, and original rural water-town charm, less commercialized than some famous peers.
items.history: With a history of over 2,500 years, Luzhi was named during the Ming Dynasty. It preserves dozens of ancient bridges from the Song, Ming, and Qing dynasties and traditional water-town living scenes.
items.tips: Half-day from Suzhou; weekend food stalls.

items.description: A scenic peninsula extending into Taihu Lake, known for lush hills, clear lake views, cherry blossoms in spring, and natural landscapes blending mountains and water.
items.history: The area was developed as a scenic spot in the early 20th century. It became a national scenic area due to its unique geographical shape resembling a turtle's head and its magnificent views of Taihu Lake.
items.tips: Cherry peak late March–April; ferries to islands.

items.description: A large Buddhist cultural scenic area centered on the giant Lingshan Grand Buddha statue, including Buddhist palaces, halls, gardens, and cultural performances.
items.history: Built in the 1990s on the site of ancient Xiangfu Temple, which dated to the Tang Dynasty. The Lingshan Grand Buddha was completed in 1997, becoming one of the largest Buddha statues in China and a key Buddhist cultural site in the Yangtze Delta.
items.tips: Large site—shuttle buses; religious dress respect.

items.description: A long, narrow scenic lake with classical pavilions, stone bridges, willow trees, and gardens. It is known for its graceful, slender shape and poetic scenery.
items.history: Formed gradually from river channels in the Sui and Tang dynasties, it flourished as a royal and literati resort during the Qing Dynasty. Emperors Kangxi and Qianlong visited many times, boosting its construction and fame.
items.tips: Spring willows famous; boat tours leisurely.

items.description: Three scenic mountains along the Yangtze River in Zhenjiang, each with temples, historic sites, legends, and river views, combining natural scenery and cultural relics.
items.history: Famous since the Six Dynasties. Jinshan Temple is linked to legends of Bai Suzhen; the island-temple setting faces the Yangtze.
items.tips: Ferry views; combine with nearby Xijin ferry.

items.description: Three scenic mountains along the Yangtze River in Zhenjiang, each with temples, historic sites, legends, and river views, combining natural scenery and cultural relics.
items.history: Famous since the Six Dynasties. Jiaoshan is known for ancient stone carvings and forested slopes above the river.
items.tips: Boat access only; half-day visit.

items.description: Three scenic mountains along the Yangtze River in Zhenjiang, each with temples, historic sites, legends, and river views, combining natural scenery and cultural relics.
items.history: Famous since the Six Dynasties. Beigu Mountain is known for historical stories from the Three Kingdoms period and river panoramas.
items.tips: Short climb; combine with Xijin historic street.

items.description: A large wetland ecosystem with lakes, marshes, reeds, and wetlands, offering eco-tourism, bird watching, and water sports.
items.history: Historically a natural wetland formed by river floods. It was designated a national wetland park to protect biodiversity and became an ecological tourist destination in central Jiangsu.
items.tips: Mosquito season in summer; spring/autumn pleasant.

items.description: China's first large-scale comprehensive museum invested and built by the state. Located at the foot of Zijin Mountain in Nanjing, it features a grand Liao-dynasty-style palace main hall. Adopting a 'One Museum, Six Halls' layout, it houses over 420,000 cultural relics spanning from prehistory to modern times, serving as a key institution for history, art, and cultural heritage.
items.history: Founded in 1933 as the preparatory office of the National Central Museum, with Cai Yuanpei as the first council chairman. Construction was interrupted by the Anti-Japanese War and resumed post-1945. Renamed National Nanjing Museum in 1950 and finalized as Nanjing Museum in 1959. Its history mirrors the development of China's modern museum cause.
items.tips: Reserve online; closed Mondays; plan half a day—galleries are extensive.

items.description: The mausoleum of the Hongwu Emperor, founder of the Ming dynasty, and his empress. Located at the southern foot of Mount Zijin in Nanjing, it is the first Ming tomb to receive nationwide protection and set the architectural model for subsequent Ming and Qing imperial tombs. Its layout features a winding sacred way and a square citadel, harmoniously integrating with the natural mountain terrain.
items.history: Construction began in 1381 and was completed in 1405. It was the joint burial site of Zhu Yuanzhang (Emperor Hongwu) and Empress Ma. During the Taiping Rebellion, the wooden structures were destroyed, but the stone architecture remained largely intact. Major restoration took place in the late 19th and late 20th centuries.
items.tips: Combine with the nearby Plum Blossom Hill (especially February–March); allow 2–3 hours; wear comfortable walking shoes.

provinces.description: Jiangsu is located in the Yangtze River Delta, known as 'Land of Fish and Rice' with developed economy and rich culture.
provinces.history: It was the territory of Wu and Yue States. It has many ancient capitals and water towns, and is an important part of Jiangnan culture.
provinces.cuisine: Nanjing Salted Duck, Yangzhou Fried Rice, Wuxi Spareribs, Squirrel Mandarin Fish

items.description: A world-famous freshwater lake surrounded by hills, parks, pagodas, temples, and gardens. It is a symbol of Hangzhou with classic ten scenic views.
items.history: Admired by poets and scholars since the Tang Dynasty. Emperors and officials built dikes, pagodas, and temples over centuries. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a cultural icon of China.
items.tips: Weekends crowded; sunrise bike rides calmer.

items.description: A well-preserved water town divided into East and West Scenic Zones, with canals, stone bridges, ancient houses, and traditional crafts. It hosts the annual World Internet Conference.
items.history: Founded over 1,300 years ago, it prospered in the Ming and Qing dynasties. Restored in the late 20th century, it became a top cultural water town and an international conference venue.
items.tips: West zone ticketed; evening performances extra.

items.description: An ancient water town with long covered corridors, stone alleys, bridges, and a peaceful atmosphere, preserving authentic water-town living scenes.
items.history: Built during the Spring and Autumn Period and Warring States Period, it matured in the Ming and Qing dynasties. Its covered corridors are a unique architectural feature.
items.tips: Avoid major holidays; night entry sometimes discounted.

items.description: A historic water town with a blend of Chinese and Western architecture, former wealthy merchant residences, canals, and classical gardens.
items.history: Flourished in the Ming and Qing dynasties due to silk trade. Rich merchants built luxurious houses combining Western design with traditional Chinese gardens, creating a unique style.
items.tips: Combine with Huzhou day trip.

items.description: A sacred Buddhist mountain on an island, one of China's four major Buddhist mountains, dedicated to Guanyin Bodhisattva, with numerous temples and natural sea views.
items.history: Buddhist construction began in the Tang Dynasty and flourished in the Song, Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties. It has been a major pilgrimage site for Guanyin worship for over a thousand years.
items.tips: Ferry weather dependent; no private cars on island.

items.description: A famous granite mountain scenic area known for strange peaks, steep cliffs, waterfalls, caves, and unique volcanic landforms.
items.history: Formed by ancient volcanic activity, it was named and developed as a scenic spot over 1,500 years ago. It has been praised by writers and travelers since the Northern and Southern Dynasties.
items.tips: Multi-day ticket; slippery after rain.

items.description: A large man-made lake formed by a hydropower dam, with thousands of forested islands, clear water, and recreational water activities.
items.history: Created in 1959 with the completion of the Xin'an River Dam. The submerged ancient cities and unique island landscape turned it into a major eco-tourism destination.
items.tips: Choose cruise routes carefully—some islands touristy.

items.description: The largest film and television studio in Asia, with replicas of imperial palaces, ancient cities, streets, and international-style sets, used for thousands of movies and dramas.
items.history: Founded in 1996 to support film production. It expanded rapidly to include multiple theme bases and became known as "China's Hollywood."
items.tips: Allow full day; shows timed—check schedules.

items.description: A rare urban secondary wetland with rivers, ponds, reeds, ancient villages, and ecological leisure areas, close to downtown Hangzhou.
items.history: Human settlement dates back over 1,800 years. Historically a fishing and farming wetland, it was protected and developed as a national wetland park in the 21st century.
items.tips: Electric boats reduce walking; mosquitos summer.

items.description: A renowned ancient Buddhist temple surrounded by lush Feilai Peak hills, with magnificent halls, stone carvings, and deep cultural heritage.
items.history: Founded in 328 AD during the Eastern Jin Dynasty by an Indian monk. It is one of the oldest and most important Buddhist temples in southern China, rebuilt many times after wars.
items.tips: Morning incense heavy; Feilai Peak ticket separate.

items.description: A large theme park reproducing the lifestyle and architecture of the Song Dynasty, with performances, folk activities, and ancient-style streets.
items.history: Built in 1996 based on the famous painting Along the River During the Qingming Festival. It focuses on Song Dynasty culture and immersive folk experiences.
items.tips: Show tickets sell out—reserve seats.

items.description: A mountainous scenic area with waterfalls, canyons, temples, and religious significance as the origin of the Tiantai Buddhist sect.
items.history: Buddhist development began in the Southern Dynasties. The Guoqing Temple was founded in the Sui Dynasty as the headquarters of Tiantai Buddhism. It has both natural beauty and religious importance.
items.tips: Mountain roads winding; misty mornings.

items.description: A dramatic mountain scenic area with steep quartz peaks, clouds, valleys, and suspension bridges, known for its otherworldly natural landscape.
items.history: Formed by geological tectonic movements, it was historically praised by ancient literati but became widely known as a scenic spot in modern times for its unique peak forest.
items.tips: Cableways; weather can close bridges.

items.description: A scenic river valley with clear water, ancient villages, karst hills, bamboo forests, and traditional folk houses, preserving rural tranquility.
items.history: Human activity dates to ancient times. The area preserves dozens of ancient villages from the Ming and Qing dynasties. It became famous for its natural scenery and cultural villages in the late 20th century.
items.tips: Summer swimming; autumn harvest scenery.

items.description: A cultural memorial area in Shaoxing including Lu Xun's former residence, memorial hall, Baicao Garden, and Sanwei Study, showcasing the writer's early life.
items.history: The buildings date to the late Qing Dynasty. Lu Xun lived here in his childhood. The site was protected and opened as a memorial in the 1950s to commemorate the great modern Chinese writer.
items.tips: Combine with Shaoxing canal boat rides; busy on weekends—book if timed entry applies.

provinces.description: Zhejiang is a coastal province in East China, known as 'Home of Silk' and 'Land of Fish and Rice'.
provinces.history: It was the State of Yue in ancient times. Hangzhou was the capital of the Southern Song Dynasty. It has West Lake and many ancient water towns.
provinces.cuisine: Dongpo Pork, West Lake Vinegar Fish, Longjing Shrimp, Beggar's Chicken, Ningbo Tangyuan

items.description: A world-famous mountain known for four wonders: strange pine trees, grotesque rocks, sea of clouds, and hot springs. It has steep peaks and breathtaking scenery.
items.history: Appreciated by travelers and painters since the Tang Dynasty. It became a symbol of Chinese landscape painting. A UNESCO World Heritage Site and global geopark.
items.tips: Stay overnight on summit for sunrise; book lodges early.

items.addressFull: Yi County, Huangshan City, Anhui, China
items.description: A well-preserved ancient Huizhou village with a unique water system, black-tiled white houses, classical courtyards, and beautiful reflections in water.
items.history: Built in the Southern Song Dynasty, it was designed with a complete water network for daily use and irrigation. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the Ancient Villages in Southern Anhui.
items.tips: Crowded midday—dawn and dusk best for photos.

items.addressFull: Yi County, Huangshan City, Anhui, China
items.description: Another outstanding ancient Huizhou village with orderly streets, ancestral halls, exquisite wood carvings, and traditional Hui-style architecture.
items.history: Founded in the Northern Song Dynasty and expanded in the Ming and Qing dynasties by wealthy Huizhou merchants. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with intact ancient village layout.
items.tips: Often combined same-day with Hongcun by car.

items.description: One of China's four sacred Buddhist mountains, dedicated to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, with many ancient temples, nunneries, and natural mountain scenery.
items.history: Buddhist construction began in the Eastern Jin Dynasty and flourished in the Tang Dynasty. It has been a major pilgrimage site for over 1,600 years.
items.tips: Pilgrim crowds on festivals; cableways shorten hikes.

items.description: A national scenic area with granite peaks, deep valleys, waterfalls, and cultural relics, also known as Wan Mountain, the origin of Anhui's short name "Wan."
items.history: Famous since the Han Dynasty. Emperor Wu of Han worshipped the mountain. It has both natural beauty and important Taoist and Buddhist heritage.
items.tips: Steep sections; weather changes fast.

items.addressFull: She County, Huangshan City, Anhui, China
items.description: A well-preserved historic city that was the political and cultural center of ancient Huizhou, with city walls, government offices, ancestral halls, and traditional streets.
items.history: Built in the Qin Dynasty, it served as the capital of Huizhou for over 2,000 years. It preserves the complete urban layout and architecture of Huizhou culture.
items.tips: City ticket includes museums; evenings quieter.

items.description: A water town at the junction of three rivers, with ancient bridges, streets, and battle sites from the Taiping Rebellion.
items.history: Formed during the Three Kingdoms period and prospered in the Ming and Qing dynasties. It is known for its water-town scenery and modern revolutionary history.
items.tips: Weekend food stalls; smaller than Hongcun.

items.addressFull: Xiuning County, Huangshan City, Anhui, China
items.description: A famous Taoist mountain with red cliffs, inscriptions, Taoist temples, and unique Danxia landform.
items.history: Developed as a Taoist sanctuary in the Tang Dynasty. It has numerous cliff inscriptions and temples, making it a key site of Taoism in southern China.
items.tips: Often paired with Huangshan trips.

items.description: A well-preserved natural ecological area with virgin forests, waterfalls, rare plants, and animals, known as "East China's last primeval forest."
items.history: Historically a remote mountainous area, it was protected as a natural reserve in modern times to preserve biodiversity and original ecological scenery.
items.tips: Remote—limited services; leeches in wet season.

items.addressFull: She County, Huangshan City, Anhui, China
items.description: A river section with green hills, clear water, fishing boats, ancient villages, and misty scenery, like a traditional Chinese landscape painting.
items.history: The Xin'an River has nurtured Huizhou culture for thousands of years. The scenic gallery was developed to showcase the natural and cultural beauty of the river basin.
items.tips: Spring photography peak; boats timed.

items.description: A scenic cliff on the Yangtze River with historic temples, poetry inscriptions, and panoramic river views, famous in Chinese literary history.
items.history: A famous scenic spot since the Six Dynasties. Many poets including Li Bai wrote poems here. It has witnessed numerous historical events and battles.
items.tips: Combine with Ma'anshan city museum.

items.addressFull: Huizhou District, Huangshan City, Anhui, China
items.description: An ancient Huizhou village designed according to the Eight Trigrams layout, with well-preserved Hui-style buildings and a unique spatial structure.
items.history: Founded in the Three Kingdoms period and planned in the Tang Dynasty using fengshui principles. It preserves rare ancient village layout and architecture.
items.tips: Stone lanes can be wet; hire a local guide to decode hall names; combine with Huangshan trips.

provinces.description: Anhui is famous for Huangshan Mountain, Huizhou culture and the historical Huizhou merchants.
provinces.history: It has a long history of cultural development. Huizhou culture is one of the three major regional cultures in China. It has many world-famous ancient villages.
provinces.cuisine: Huizhou Stinky Mandarin Fish, Hairy Tofu, Wuwei Salted Duck, Huainan Beef Soup

items.description: A car-free island near Xiamen with Western-style villas, gardens, piano museums, beaches, and quiet lanes, known as "Piano Island."
items.history: Developed as a foreign settlement in the late 19th century, with consulates and villas built by Western countries. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its unique architectural mix.
items.tips: Ferry tickets timed; weekends crowded.

items.description: A scenic area with Danxia landform, bamboo rafting on the Jiuqu Stream, tea plantations (Da Hong Pao), and Taoist and Confucian sites.
items.history: A cultural and religious center for over 2,000 years. It is the birthplace of authentic oolong tea. A UNESCO mixed cultural and natural World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Rafting tickets sell out—reserve; tea culture nearby.

items.description: Large fortified circular and square earthen buildings, unique communal residences of the Hakka people, with thick walls and compact internal layout.
items.history: Built between the 12th and 20th centuries by Hakka communities for defense and communal living. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site representing Hakka culture.
items.tips: Stay inside a tulou for full experience; roads mountainous.

items.description: Large fortified circular and square earthen buildings, unique communal residences of the Hakka people, with thick walls and compact internal layout.
items.history: Built between the 12th and 20th centuries by Hakka communities for defense and communal living. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site representing Hakka culture.
items.tips: Viewpoints require short hikes; rainy steps slippery.

items.description: A historic block in Fuzhou preserving Ming and Qing courtyard houses, ancestral halls, and traditional streets, the birthplace of many historical figures.
items.history: Formed during the Tang and Song dynasties and flourished in the Ming and Qing dynasties. It was the residential area of Fuzhou's elite and retains authentic ancient urban texture.
items.tips: Evening lantern walks; food street busy.

items.description: A mountain scenic area with stone statues, temples, springs, and inscriptions, a famous religious and cultural site in southern Fujian.
items.history: Development began in the Qin Dynasty. It features a huge ancient stone statue of Laozi from the Song Dynasty and integrates Buddhist, Taoist, and Confucian relics.
items.tips: Half-day hike; combine with Quanzhou UNESCO old town.

items.description: A coastal mountain with strange granite peaks, caves, sea views, and legends, known as the "Fairy Mountain on the Sea."
items.history: Human activity and temple construction date to the Han Dynasty. It has been a famous scenic and religious site for over 2,000 years.
items.tips: Fog common; wear grippy shoes.

items.description: The holy island of Mazu, the sea goddess, with Mazu temples, beaches, and coastal scenery, a pilgrimage site for coastal Chinese.
items.history: The ancestral Mazu Temple was built in the Song Dynasty. Mazu worship spread across coastal regions and overseas, making the island a cultural center for Mazu belief.
items.tips: Ferry wind cancellations; temple etiquette.

items.description: A well-preserved coastal military city built for defense, with stone walls, beaches, and stone carving culture.
items.history: Constructed in the Ming Dynasty to resist Japanese pirates. It is one of the best-preserved coastal fortresses in China and a center of Hui'an stone carving.
items.tips: Windy coast; combine with nearby beaches.

items.description: A scenic village with ancient banyan trees, tulou buildings, cobblestone paths, and a river, made famous by movies.
items.history: Formed over hundreds of years ago, it combines Hakka tulou and southern Fujian village scenery. It gained popularity after being featured in several films.
items.tips: Film-famous—tourist buses frequent.

items.description: A Danxia landform scenic area with canyons, lakes, caves, and ancient villages, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.history: Formed by geological evolution over millions of years. Human settlement dates to the Tang Dynasty. It preserves intact Danxia landscapes and cultural relics.
items.tips: UNESCO nature site—boat tours weather dependent.

items.description: A Danxia mountain with steep red cliffs, narrow valleys, waterfalls, and unique peak shapes.
items.history: Appreciated as a scenic spot since the Song Dynasty. Its distinctive Danxia landform and natural beauty attract many visitors.
items.tips: Half-day outing; summer heat.

items.description: A historic old town in Quanzhou, Fujian, known as 'Zaitun City' (Cotton City). It is the core area of 'Quanzhou: UNESCO World Heritage Site of China's World Marine Trade Center in the Song and Yuan Dynasties'. Featuring a well-preserved ancient urban pattern, traditional southern Fujian architecture, numerous cultural relics, and a strong blend of religious and folk culture, it is a vivid showcase of the ancient Maritime Silk Road.
items.history: With a history dating back over 1,300 years, Quanzhou was established as a city in the Tang Dynasty (around 700 AD). It flourished as the 'No. 1 Port in the East' during the Song and Yuan dynasties, a hub for international trade and cultural exchange. The old town preserves landmarks like West Street, East and West Pagodas, and Deji Gate, witnessing its glorious past as a multicultural maritime metropolis.
items.tips: Walk Kaiyuan Temple, Qingjing Mosque, and Guandi lanes; respect worship sites; summer is hot and humid.

provinces.description: Fujian is a coastal province, the starting point of the ancient Maritime Silk Road, with rich Minnan culture.
provinces.history: Quanzhou was the world's largest port in the Song and Yuan Dynasties. It has a large number of overseas Chinese and unique coastal culture.
provinces.cuisine: Buddha Jumps Over the Wall, Shaxian Snacks, Fuzhou Fish Balls, Oyster Omelet

items.description: A famous mountain with waterfalls, clouds, temples, villas, and cool summer climate, a symbol of Chinese mountain culture.
items.history: Admired since the Qin and Han dynasties. Poets like Li Bai wrote famous poems about it. It has numerous historical sites and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Fog common; tickets cover multiple zones—plan days.

items.description: A Taoist mountain with unique granite peaks, pine trees, clouds, and well-preserved natural scenery.
items.history: Taoist development began in the Jin Dynasty. Its spectacular peak forest resembles Chinese landscape paintings. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Weather closes glass decks; stay summit for sunrise.

items.description: A rural area known for yellow rapeseed flowers in spring, ancient Huizhou villages, black-tiled white houses, and idyllic scenery.
items.history: Historically part of Huizhou, it preserves typical Hui-style villages. Its rural landscape and seasonal flowers made it a famous cultural and eco-tourism spot.
items.tips: Peak blossom weeks crowded—book homestays.

items.description: One of China's Three Great Towers South of the Yangtze, with classic Chinese architecture, overlooking the Gan River, famous through ancient poetry.
items.history: First built in the Tang Dynasty. It became immortalized by Wang Bo's famous poem Tengwang Ge Xu. Rebuilt many times, the current structure follows ancient architectural style.
items.tips: Evening lighting; elevator inside modern structure.

items.description: A Taoist sacred mountain with Danxia landform, bamboo rafting, and Taoist temples, the birthplace of Taoism's Zhengyi Sect.
items.history: Founded as a Taoist center in the Eastern Han Dynasty by Zhang Daoling. It combines unique Danxia scenery and profound Taoist heritage.
items.tips: UNESCO mixed site; summer heat and humidity.
