items.description: A mountainous revolutionary base area with forests, waterfalls, and revolutionary memorial sites, known as the "Cradle of the Chinese Revolution."
items.history: In 1927, Mao Zedong established the first rural revolutionary base here. It is now a major red tourism site combining nature and revolutionary history.
items.tips: Political sites plus nature trails.

items.description: China's largest freshwater lake, with wetlands, migratory birds, reed marshes, and seasonal water-level changes.
items.history: A natural lake formed thousands of years ago. It is an important wetland and habitat for wintering migratory birds, playing a key ecological role.
items.tips: Winter birding best; water level varies seasonally.

items.description: A high mountain with alpine meadows, sea of clouds, sunrise views, and hiking trails, popular among outdoor enthusiasts.
items.history: Historically a remote mountain with Taoist temples. Its vast meadows at high altitude have made it a famous hiking and camping destination.
items.tips: Camping on ridge—check weather wind.

items.description: A scenic mountain with waterfalls, hot springs, forests, and a cool climate, suitable for leisure and health tourism.
items.history: Named for its crescent-shaped peaks. It has been a local scenic spot for centuries and developed into a modern resort with hot spring facilities.
items.tips: Spa hotels; fog days limit views.

items.nameCn: 景德镇古窑民俗博览区
items.nameEn: Jingdezhen Ancient Kiln Folk Customs Museum
items.description: A cultural area showcasing ancient porcelain-making techniques, historic kilns, workshops, and ceramic art.
items.history: Jingdezhen has been China's "Porcelain Capital" since the Song Dynasty. The museum preserves ancient kiln sites and traditional ceramic craftsmanship.
items.tips: Hands-on workshops cost extra; fragile ceramics shipping.

items.description: A quiet ancient town with green mountains, clear rivers, old kiln sites, and traditional houses, historically a porcelain-producing area.
items.history: Flourished in the Tang and Song dynasties as a porcelain-making center. It retains ancient workshops, streets, and natural ecological scenery.
items.tips: Half-day from Jingdezhen; rural roads.

provinces.description: Jiangxi is known for its beautiful landscapes, red revolutionary culture and prosperous literary history.
provinces.history: It has a long cultural history. The Nanchang Uprising broke out here in 1927. It has Lushan Mountain, Jinggangshan and other famous scenic spots.
provinces.cuisine: Three-Cup Chicken, Nanchang Rice Noodles, Clay Pot Soup, Poyang Lake Silver Fish

items.description: China's most sacred mountain, the leading of the Five Great Mountains, with stone inscriptions, temples, and a long history of imperial worship.
items.history: Emperors from the Qin and Han dynasties held Fengshan ceremonies here. It has over 2,000 years of cultural history and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Night hike popular—bring torch; summit cold.

items.description: A complex of ancient buildings honoring Confucius, including the Confucius Temple, his family's mansion, and the family cemetery.
items.history: First built in 478 BC after Confucius' death. Expanded over dynasties, it became the largest Confucian complex in the world. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Combine ticket with Kong Mansion and Kong Forest.

items.description: A complex of ancient buildings honoring Confucius, including the Confucius Temple, his family's mansion, and the family cemetery.
items.history: First built in 478 BC after Confucius' death. Expanded over dynasties, it became the largest Confucian complex in the world. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Linked path with temple; crowded tour groups.

items.description: A complex of ancient buildings honoring Confucius, including the Confucius Temple, his family's mansion, and the family cemetery.
items.history: First built in 478 BC after Confucius' death. Expanded over dynasties, it became the largest Confucian complex in the world. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Electric carts optional; respectful behavior.

items.description: A group of famous springs and lakes in Jinan, known as the "City of Springs," with clear springs, parks, and traditional pavilions.
items.history: The springs have been famous since the Spring and Autumn Period. Baotu Spring was named by Emperor Qianlong. It is the symbol of Jinan's spring culture.
items.tips: Dry spells reduce flow—check local reports.

items.description: A group of famous springs and lakes in Jinan, known as the "City of Springs," with clear springs, parks, and traditional pavilions.
items.history: The springs have been famous since the Spring and Autumn Period. Baotu Spring was named by Emperor Qianlong. It is the symbol of Jinan's spring culture.
items.tips: Boat rides; summer lotus bloom.

items.description: A coastal island with naval museums, historic sites of the First Sino-Japanese War, and natural scenery.
items.history: The main base of the Qing Dynasty Beiyang Fleet. It witnessed the 1895 Sino-Japanese War. Now a national patriotism education base and scenic spot.
items.tips: Ferry wind cancellations; half-day minimum.

items.description: A famous coastal Taoist mountain with cliffs, sea views, temples, springs, and pure spring water.
items.history: Taoist development began in the Han Dynasty. It is known as a "Fairy Mountain on the Sea" and produces famous Laoshan spring water.
items.tips: Separate scenic zones—plan route.

items.description: A well-preserved historic city with ancient streets, gates, temples, and folk culture, once a key political center in Shandong.
items.history: With a history of over 2,200 years, it served as a provincial capital in ancient China. It retains complete ancient urban layout and traditional architecture.
items.tips: Free core; museums small.

items.description: A mountainous area with forests, waterfalls, red revolutionary sites, and rural scenery, a symbol of Yimeng spirit.
items.history: Known for revolutionary history during the Chinese Civil War. It combines natural ecological scenery and red tourism resources.
items.tips: Spread out—need car between sites.

items.description: A historic pavilion on a cliff overlooking the Bohai Sea, famous for mirages and legends of the Eight Immortals.
items.history: Built in the Northern Song Dynasty. It is linked to immortality legends and has been a famous coastal scenic spot for over 900 years.
items.tips: Ferry to islands weather dependent.

items.description: A large scenic area with Buddhist statues, gardens, forests, and leisure facilities, integrating religion and tourism.
items.history: Developed in modern times on a historic site. It features a large Buddha statue and comprehensive recreational landscapes.
items.tips: Commercialized; full day if including all zones.

items.description: A reconstructed water town on the Grand Canal, with canals, bridges, and battle sites of the Taierzhuang Campaign.
items.history: Historically a prosperous canal town. Destroyed in war, it was rebuilt to restore ancient canal culture and commemorate the 1938 battle.
items.tips: Evening performances; ticket includes entry.

items.description: A high-quality coastal beach with clean sand, clear water, and modern leisure facilities.
items.history: Developed as a modern coastal resort in the late 20th century. It is known for its excellent natural beach conditions.
items.tips: Jellyfish season alerts; cold water spring.

provinces.description: Shandong is the birthplace of Confucian culture, known as 'Land of Qi and Lu', with Taishan Mountain as a sacred mountain.
provinces.history: It is the hometown of Confucius and Mencius. Qufu's Confucius Sites are world cultural heritages. It has a long history of civilization.
provinces.cuisine: Dezhou Braised Chicken, Jinan Sweet and Sour Carp, Zibo Barbecue, Qingdao Beer

items.description: One of China's greatest Buddhist cave temple complexes, with thousands of stone Buddha statues carved into limestone cliffs along the Yi River.
items.history: Construction began in the Northern Wei Dynasty and continued for over 500 years through Sui and Tang. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site representing peak Buddhist art.
items.tips: West Hill crowded; evening lighting special tours.

items.description: The legendary birthplace of Shaolin Kung Fu and Chan Buddhism, with martial arts performances, pagoda forests, and ancient halls.
items.history: Founded in 495 AD during the Northern Wei Dynasty. It became famous for Chan Buddhism and martial arts, especially after historical legends spread.
items.tips: Commercialized surrounds; arrive early to beat tours.

items.description: A spectacular canyon scenic area with waterfalls, clear springs, red cliffs, and unique geological landforms.
items.history: Formed by geological movements over billions of years. It became a national geopark for its rare geological features and beautiful scenery.
items.tips: Crowded narrow gorges—go early.

items.description: A large theme park reproducing the scenery and lifestyle of the Northern Song Dynasty, based on Along the River During the Qingming Festival.
items.history: Built in 1998 in Kaifeng, the ancient capital of the Northern Song Dynasty. It immerses visitors in Song Dynasty urban culture and folk customs.
items.tips: Costumed shows timed; hot summers.

items.description: The ruins of the late Shang Dynasty capital, with oracle bone sites, royal tombs, and archaeological museums.
items.history: The capital of the Shang Dynasty over 3,300 years ago. It is where oracle bones were first discovered, proving China's earliest written language. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Museum + palace foundations—guides add context.

items.description: The central sacred mountain of China's Five Great Mountains, with forested peaks, temples, and historic sites.
items.history: A sacred mountain since ancient times. It is home to Shaolin Temple and has important historical and religious significance.
items.tips: Combine with Shaolin; cableways on some routes.

items.description: A Taoist mountain named after Laozi, with golden summits, sea of clouds, snow scenes, and Taoist architecture.
items.history: Legend says Laozi cultivated here in ancient times. Developed as a Taoist site, it became famous for its stunning golden summit and natural scenery.
items.tips: Winter snow scenes; ropeways may close.

items.description: A high-mountain scenic area with forests, waterfalls, clouds, and cool climate, a summer resort.
items.history: A remote natural mountain protected as a forest park. It is known for its high vegetation coverage and comfortable climate.
items.tips: Summer cool; fog reduces views.

items.description: A large limestone cave with spectacular stalactites, stalagmites, and underground rivers, known as "The First Cave in North China."
items.history: Formed over hundreds of millions of years. Discovered and developed as a tourist cave in modern times for its magnificent karst landscape.
items.tips: Slippery floors; jacket inside.

items.description: A deep canyon with waterfalls, clear pools, red rock walls, and hiking paths, a typical Danxia canyon.
items.history: Formed by long-term river erosion. It is praised for its beautiful water scenery and steep canyon landform.
items.tips: Flash flood risk in rain—follow closures.

items.description: An enormous man-made water conservancy project built on steep mountains, a symbol of self-reliance and hard work.
items.history: Constructed manually by local people from 1960 to 1969 to solve water shortages. It is now a patriotic education and sightseeing site.
items.tips: Mountain roads; red tourism narrative.

items.description: A mountain with strange peaks, waterfalls, azaleas in spring, and winter snow scenery.
items.history: A natural scenic area with a long history of literati visits. It is known for its unique peak shapes and seasonal landscapes.
items.tips: Cableways; winter skiing zone.

provinces.description: Henan is located in the Central Plains, the core birthplace of Chinese civilization, with many ancient capitals.
provinces.history: Many ancient dynasties established capitals here. It has four ancient capitals: Luoyang, Kaifeng, Anyang and Zhengzhou. It has a long historical heritage.
provinces.cuisine: Hulatang, Daokou Braised Chicken, Luoyang Water Banquet, Kaifeng Soup Dumplings

items.description: A world-famous Taoist mountain and martial arts center, with ancient Taoist temples, golden halls, and the origin of Tai Chi martial arts.
items.history: Taoist construction began in the Tang Dynasty and peaked in the Ming Dynasty under imperial support. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for Taoist culture and architecture.
items.tips: Mountain buses required; steep climbs.

items.description: One of China's Three Great Towers South of the Yangtze, overlooking the Yangtze River, famous through classical poetry.
items.history: First built in the Three Kingdoms period. Immortalized by Tang poems. Destroyed and rebuilt many times; the current tower follows Qing Dynasty style.
items.tips: Evening lighting; elevator to upper floors.

items.description: A large natural reserve with primeval forests, rare animals (including legend of "Wild Man"), waterfalls, and high biodiversity.
items.history: Named after the mythical Shennong who tasted herbs. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a critical ecological protection area.
items.tips: Cool summers; misty; leeches in wet season.

items.description: The world's largest hydropower project, with a massive dam, ship locks, viewing platforms, and exhibition centers.
items.history: Construction began in 1994 and was completed in 2006. It serves flood control, power generation, and navigation, becoming a modern engineering landmark.
items.tips: Security screening; weather cancels platforms.

items.description: A large urban lake in Wuhan with parks, gardens, wetlands, and recreational areas, one of China's biggest urban lakes.
items.history: Formed by natural water systems. Developed as a city park in the 20th century, it is Wuhan's major leisure and ecological scenic spot.
items.tips: Spring blossom crowds; rent bikes.

items.description: A spectacular karst canyon with steep cliffs, plank roads, waterfalls, and unique peak forests in western Hubei.
items.history: Formed by geological movements and erosion. It preserves pristine karst scenery and is known as "China's Grand Canyon."
items.tips: Fog and rain common; steep stairs.

items.description: A historic site commemorating the famous Battle of Red Cliffs, with monuments, temples, and cultural exhibitions.
items.history: The site of the decisive Battle of Red Cliffs in 208 AD during the Three Kingdoms period. It has been memorialized for over 1,800 years.
items.tips: Historically reconstructed—manage expectations.

items.description: The imperial mausoleum of Ming Dynasty parents of Emperor Jiajing, with unique symmetrical layout and grand architecture.
items.history: Built in the 16th century during the Ming Dynasty. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and represents a special form of imperial mausoleum.
items.tips: Rural site—transport needed.

items.description: A scenic river canyon with clear water, karst peaks, caves, and boat tours, known for its picturesque landscape.
items.history: A natural river valley nurtured by the Qingjiang River. It combines karst landforms and ethnic culture in southwestern Hubei.
items.tips: Boat schedules seasonal; peak summer.

items.description: A mountainous scenic area themed on the legendary heroine Mulan, with forests, lakes, and cultural sites.
items.history: Based on the legend of Mulan, a folk heroine. The area integrates natural scenery with traditional heroic culture.
items.tips: Day trip from Wuhan; multiple sub-parks.

provinces.description: Hubei is known as the 'Thoroughfare to Nine Provinces', the core area of Chu culture, with the Three Gorges and Wudang Mountain.
provinces.history: It was the core of the ancient Chu State. It has important historical and cultural relics such as the Yellow Crane Tower and Shennongjia.
provinces.cuisine: Hot Dry Noodles, Wuchang Fish, Duck Neck, Lotus Root Soup, Sanxian Doupi

items.description: China's first national forest park, famous for towering quartz sandstone pillars, karst landscapes, lush forests, and spectacular canyon scenery. It inspired the floating mountains in the movie Avatar. The wider Wulingyuan area includes Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon and glass-bridge attractions.
items.history: Established in 1982 as China's first national forest park. In 1992, Zhangjiajie's quartz sandstone peak forest was inscribed as a UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site. It has gradually developed into an international-class mountain tourism destination.
items.tips: Crowded elevators; book tickets; fog risk.

items.description: An ancient riverside town in western Hunan with well-preserved Ming and Qing architecture, stilted houses along the Tuo River, stone alleys, and distinctive Miao and Tujia ethnic culture. It is known as one of China's most beautiful ancient towns.
items.history: Founded during the Qing Dynasty, it has a history of over 300 years. Historically a strategic border town and trading hub for ethnic groups. It gained nationwide fame through the writings of writer Shen Congwen.
items.tips: Night bars noisy; river pollution varies—check advisories.

items.description: One of China's Five Great Mountains (Yue), known as the 'Southern Mountain'. It features dense forests, temples, Taoist and Buddhist cultural sites, mild climate, and the famous 'Hengshan Cloud Sea'. It is a sacred mountain for both Taoism and Buddhism.
items.history: Worshiped as a sacred mountain since the Qin and Han dynasties. Many imperial emperors held ceremonies here. Major temples such as Nanyue Temple were constructed over successive dynasties.
items.tips: Pilgrim crowds on holidays; cable car option.

items.description: A long sandy island in the Xiangjiang River in Changsha, featuring parks, sculptures, gardens, and riverside scenery. It is famous for its large statue of Mao Zedong and poetic cultural significance.
items.history: Famous for Mao Zedong's poem Changsha. It has been developed as an urban scenic area since the 1950s and renovated into a national key scenic spot in the 21st century.
items.tips: Free park; evening fireworks seasonal.

items.description: The hometown of Mao Zedong, featuring his former residence, memorial hall, square statue, and revolutionary cultural relics. It is an important revolutionary education and red tourism base.
items.history: Mao Zedong was born here in 1893. It became a major revolutionary memorial site after 1949. Designated as a national key scenic area and patriotic education base.
items.tips: Security lines; respectful dress.

items.description: A steep mountain with a natural karst cave 'Heaven's Gate', a long glass walkway, cable cars, and cliffside paths. Known for misty peaks and thrilling viewing platforms.
items.history: Developed as a tourist attraction in the late 20th century. The cable car and sky walk were built to enhance tourism. It is part of the broader Zhangjiajie scenic zone.
items.tips: Weather closes glass paths; queue management strict.

items.description: A large reservoir and scenic lake with clear water, islands, misty river sections, canyons, and ecological scenery. Famous for morning fog over the Xiaodongjiang River.
items.history: Formed by the construction of Dongjiang Hydropower Station in the 1980s. Later developed into a national wetland park and ecological tourist resort.
items.tips: Sunrise boat tours start very early.

items.description: A typical Danxia landform scenic area with red sandstone peaks, natural bridges, caves, canyons, and lush vegetation. It is a UNESCO World Natural Heritage component (China Danxia).
items.history: Formed over millions of years of geological erosion. In 2010, it was inscribed as part of the China Danxia UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site.
items.tips: Steep sections; heat in summer.

items.description: A historic mountain in Changsha with temples, pavilions, and forested trails, forming one cultural landscape with Yuelu Academy at its foot. It combines natural scenery with over a thousand years of scholarship and poetry.
items.history: The mountain has been celebrated since the Tang Dynasty as a landmark overlooking the Xiang River; paths and shrines reflect long use by students and travelers visiting the academy below.
items.tips: Easy hike from university area; cable car optional.

items.description: One of China's four great ancient academies, nestled at the foot of Yuelu Mountain—an enduring center of Confucian education, Neo-Confucian debate, and classical learning.
items.history: Yuelu Academy was founded in the Northern Song Dynasty (976 AD). It has been a center of education and Neo-Confucianism for over a thousand years.
items.tips: Ticket separate from mountain park in some seasons.

items.description: A popular white-water rafting route with rapids, waterfalls, cliffs, and primeval forest scenery, known as the 'first drift under heaven'.
items.history: Developed as an adventure tourism project in the 1980s and 1990s. It quickly became a signature water sports attraction in western Hunan.
items.tips: Summer season; follow safety briefing.

items.description: A traditional Miao ethnic village surrounded by deep valleys and waterfalls, preserving folk customs, costumes, dances, and wooden architecture.
items.history: An ancient Miao settlement with hundreds of years of history. Developed as an ethnic cultural tourism spot to preserve and display minority traditions.
items.tips: Combine with nearby bridges; rural roads.

provinces.description: Hunan is known as 'Xiaoxiang', famous for Zhangjiajie, Hengshan Mountain and unique Xiang culture.
provinces.history: It was part of the Chu State in ancient times. It has rich red revolutionary culture and magnificent natural landscapes.
provinces.cuisine: Stinky Tofu, Chopped Chili Fish Head, Spicy Crayfish, Xiangxi Cured Meat

items.description: The namesake area of China's Danxia landform, featuring red sandstone peaks, gorges, natural pillars, and cliffs. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (China Danxia).
items.history: Geologically formed over 70 million years. Named the 'Danxia landform' by geologists. In 2010, it was inscribed as part of the China Danxia World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Wear sturdy shoes; summer heat and sudden rain are common. Follow marked paths in scenic zones.

items.description: A large-scale comprehensive resort including theme parks, safari parks, water parks, circus shows, hotels, and ocean parks—among Asia's top entertainment complexes (Guangzhou and Zhuhai).
items.history: Founded in 1989. Chimelong Paradise opened in 2006, followed by Zhuhai Chimelong Ocean Kingdom. It has become a leading domestic tourism brand.
items.tips: Check official hours and ticket bundles. Weekends and holidays are busiest—book online when possible.

items.description: A major safari park within the Chimelong resort in Guangzhou, with drive-through enclosures, animal shows, and family-oriented wildlife experiences.
items.history: Developed as part of Chimelong's expansion into world-class wildlife tourism alongside the group's theme parks in Guangzhou.
items.tips: Follow park rules for feeding and photos. Arrive early for popular shows and bus tours.

items.description: A famous sacred Taoist mountain known as the 'Number One Mountain in Lingnan'. It features lush forests, waterfalls, ancient temples, stone inscriptions, and rich Taoist cultural relics, offering natural scenery and cultural sightseeing.
items.history: With a history of more than 2,000 years, Luofu Mountain has been a renowned Taoist and Buddhist retreat since the Qin and Han dynasties. It was designated as a national key scenic area and later a 5A-level tourist attraction, famous for Ge Hong's alchemy and religious heritage.
items.tips: Wear comfortable hiking shoes; carry water and sun protection. Some mountain trails are steep; follow marked routes for safety.

items.description: A famous urban mountain in Guangzhou with forests, lakes, temples, viewing platforms, and cable cars—a popular recreational spot for locals.
items.history: A scenic site admired since ancient times and recorded in Tang Dynasty literature. Developed as a city park in modern times.
items.tips: Mornings are cooler; carry water. Cable cars may close in high wind.

items.description: Historic fortified multi-story towers built by overseas Chinese, combining Chinese and Western architectural styles, surrounded by traditional villages and farmland.
items.history: Built mainly in the late Qing Dynasty and early Republican era for defense against bandits. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site in 2007.
items.tips: Villages are spread out—plan transport between clusters. Respect residents' privacy.

items.description: A limestone karst scenic area with seven mountain peaks, lakes, caves, and ancient inscriptions—often called a 'fairyland on earth'.
items.history: Famous as a scenic spot since the Tang Dynasty. Many poets and scholars visited and left poems and carvings on the rocks.
items.tips: Allow half a day; boat schedules vary. Slippery paths after rain.

items.description: A large coastal island with fine beaches, clear seawater, coastal wetlands, and marine tourism—one of Guangdong's most popular beach resorts.
items.history: Historically a fishing island. Developed into a coastal tourist resort in the late 20th century.
items.tips: Watch typhoon and sea-condition alerts in summer. Sun protection essential.

items.description: A theme park featuring miniature replicas of famous global landmarks, including the Eiffel Tower, Pyramids, Taj Mahal, and more.
items.history: Opened in 1994 in Shenzhen. It was one of China's earliest large-scale theme parks representing world culture.
items.tips: Evening shows are popular—verify show times. Expect crowds on holidays.

items.description: A theme park displaying scaled-down versions of China's most famous scenic spots and historical sites in one venue.
items.history: Opened in 1989 as China's first cultural theme park. It pioneered the miniature scenic attraction model.
items.tips: Combine with nearby OCT attractions; wear comfortable shoes for walking.

items.description: A peaceful coastal beach resort in Shenzhen with clean sand, sea activities, hotels, and a marine park.
items.history: Developed as a beach resort in the 1980s during Shenzhen's rapid urbanization.
items.tips: Check beach opening rules and weather. Weekends can be crowded.

items.description: A long, clean beach with gentle waves, coastal resorts, islands, and water sports—promoted locally as 'China's Maldives'.
items.history: Developed into a high-end coastal resort area since the early 21st century.
items.tips: Summer weekends are busy; book accommodation early. Mind rip currents when swimming.

provinces.description: Guangdong is China's economic powerhouse, the forefront of reform and opening up, with distinctive Lingnan culture.
provinces.history: Guangzhou has been an important trade port since ancient times. It is a major hometown of overseas Chinese with a unique cultural style.
provinces.cuisine: White Cut Chicken, Roasted Goose, Char Siu, Cantonese Dim Sum, Chaoshan Beef Hot Pot

items.description: A world-famous river winding through limestone karst mountains, bamboo groves, and rural villages—known for 'mountains in the painting, river in the dream'.
items.history: Admired by poets and travelers for over a thousand years. The Li River scenery has been depicted in countless artworks. Core scenery is part of the South China Karst UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Mist and light change quickly—bring a light jacket. Cruise tickets sell out in peak season.

items.description: A historic pedestrian street in Yangshuo with shops, cafes, bars, handicrafts, and a multicultural backpacker atmosphere.
items.history: Formed over hundreds of years as a market street. Became an international tourist destination since the reform and opening up.
items.tips: Evenings are busiest; watch belongings in crowds.

items.description: A peaceful tributary of the Li River with gentle bamboo raft drifting, karst peaks, and rural countryside scenery.
items.history: Long used for irrigation and local transportation. Developed as a leisure rafting spot in modern tourism.
items.tips: Water levels affect rafting—confirm schedules locally.

items.description: A spectacular transboundary waterfall on the Sino-Vietnamese border, with multiple tiers and strong flow surrounded by lush mountains.
items.history: Formed by natural river geography. Developed as a border scenic area after border stabilization in the late 20th century.
items.tips: Passport may be needed for certain viewpoints; check border-area rules.

items.description: A deep canyon with primeval forest, waterfalls, underground rivers, karst caves, and rare plants.
items.history: A natural geological landscape formed over long periods. Developed for eco-tourism in recent decades.
items.tips: Slippery stone steps—wear grip shoes. Avoid visits during flood alerts.

items.description: Famous for Elephant Trunk Hill, a natural rock formation resembling an elephant drinking from the Li River—the symbol of Guilin.
items.history: The symbol of Guilin for over a thousand years. Frequently depicted in ancient Chinese paintings and poems.
items.tips: Best photos often from opposite banks; arrive early to avoid tour groups.

items.description: A volcanic island with beaches, coral reefs, sea cliffs, lighthouses, and distinctive coastal scenery.
items.history: Formed by volcanic activity. Developed as a tourist island after improved transportation in the 21st century.
items.tips: Ferry depends on sea conditions; book return tickets. Typhoon season may disrupt sailings.

items.description: A well-preserved ancient town with stone streets, ancient trees, bridges, halls, and traditional Lingnan architecture.
items.history: Founded over 1,000 years ago during the Song Dynasty. It retains authentic ancient town features.
items.tips: Overnight stays are popular; stone paths can be slick when wet.

items.description: Magnificent terraced fields on mountain slopes, built and cultivated by Zhuang and Yao ethnic groups for centuries.
items.history: First built during the Yuan Dynasty and expanded over the Ming and Qing dynasties. A masterpiece of agricultural engineering.
items.tips: Spring water-filled fields and autumn harvest are classic seasons. Steep climbs—pack light.

items.description: A magnificent karst cave with colorful stalactites, stalagmites, and rock formations known as the 'Palace of Natural Arts'.
items.history: Discovered in ancient times. Became a famous tourist cave since the 1950s and received many state leaders.
items.tips: Floors may be wet; watch steps. Guided visits are typical.

items.description: A large comprehensive park with caves, mountains, forests, historical relics, and recreational areas in central Guilin.
items.history: Developed as a scenic spot since the Tang Dynasty. One of Guilin's oldest and largest parks.
items.tips: Monkeys may approach visitors—do not feed aggressively.

provinces.description: Guangxi is the only coastal autonomous region in China, famous for 'Guilin's landscape is the finest under heaven'.
provinces.history: It has a large Zhuang population and unique karst landforms. It is a multi-ethnic integrated region with rich cultural characteristics.
provinces.cuisine: Luosifen, Guilin Rice Noodles, Lipu Taro, Nanning Old Friend Noodles

items.description: A premier beach resort with white sand, clear blue water, coral reefs, and luxury hotels—known as 'the first bay of the world'.
items.history: Developed into a high-end tourist area since the 1990s. Now a symbol of tropical coastal tourism in China.
items.tips: Sun protection and hydration are important. Check beach flags and local safety notices.

items.description: A tropical island with excellent beaches, diving sites, coral reefs, and water sports—often called 'China's Maldives'.
items.history: Formerly a small uninhabited island. Developed into a top island resort in the 21st century.
items.tips: Ferry schedules depend on weather. Book tickets in advance during holidays.

items.description: A coastal scenic area with large rocks inscribed with Tianya and Haijiao, symbolizing the remotest end of the world.
items.history: A poetic landmark since ancient times. Inscriptions were added in the Qing Dynasty. Now a cultural symbol of Hainan.
items.tips: Midday sun can be intense—bring shade and water. Expect crowds during peak travel seasons.

items.addressFull: Lingshui Li Autonomous County, Hainan, China
items.description: A tropical island with clear waters, beaches, diving, marine animal interactions, and cliff scenery.
items.history: Developed as a tourist island in the early 21st century. Known for marine tourism.
items.tips: Check boat schedules and sea conditions. Windy days may affect departures.

items.description: A large Buddhist cultural zone featuring a giant Guanyin statue by the sea, temples, gardens, and coastal scenery.
items.history: Built in the late 20th century to promote Buddhist culture and coastal tourism. The 108-meter Guanyin statue was completed in 2005.
items.tips: Dress respectfully in temple areas. Large site—wear comfortable shoes and plan half a day.

items.nameCn: 呀诺达雨林文化旅游区
items.addressFull: Baoting Li and Miao Autonomous County, Hainan, China
items.description: A tropical rainforest park with canopy walks, waterfalls, exotic plants, and ethnic cultural performances (Yanoda).
items.history: Established as an eco-tourism rainforest park in the 21st century.
items.tips: Rain is possible any season—bring a light rain jacket and non-slip shoes.

items.addressFull: Baoting Li and Miao Autonomous County, Hainan, China
items.description: An ethnic cultural village showcasing Li and Miao traditions, ancient weaving, tattoos, stilt houses, and folk customs.
items.history: Preserves the original culture of Hainan's indigenous Li people. Developed as an ethnic tourism site.
items.tips: Respect local customs during shows and village visits. Allow half a day for the full route.

items.description: A historic street with arcade-style buildings blending Chinese and Western architectural features, reflecting overseas Chinese culture.
items.history: Built in the late 19th and early 20th centuries by returned overseas Chinese. A national historical and cultural district.
items.tips: Evenings are lively; watch for scooters on shared streets.

items.description: China's coastal space launch site, used for heavy-lift rocket launches—open for tourism and science education where permitted.
items.history: Completed and put into use in 2016. It is China's fourth and most advanced space launch center.
items.tips: Launch viewing depends on official schedules and safety zones—verify access rules before traveling.

items.description: A group of pristine tropical islands with crystal-clear water, white sand, coral reefs, and rich marine life.
items.history: Part of China's South China Sea territory since ancient times. Opened for regulated tourism in modern times.
items.tips: Travel requires authorized tours or transport only—check the latest regulations and weather.

provinces.description: Hainan is China's southernmost tropical island province and a free trade port with unique coastal scenery.
provinces.history: It is China's largest special economic zone. It has rich tropical resources and coastal tourism scenery such as Sanya.
provinces.cuisine: Wenchang Chicken, Jiaji Duck, Hele Crab, Qingbuliang, Coconut Rice

items.addressFull: Zhangzha Town, Jiuzhaigou County, Ngawa, Sichuan, China
items.description: A fairyland-like valley with colorful lakes, waterfalls, snow-capped mountains, and forests—known as 'a fairyland on earth'.
items.history: Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1992. Suffered an earthquake in 2017 and reopened after reconstruction.
items.tips: Altitude and weather vary by zone—dress in layers. Shuttle buses link main valleys; plan a full day.

items.description: Famous for travertine pools in bright blue, yellow, and green colors, snow mountains, and forest scenery.
items.history: Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site with Jiuzhaigou in 1992.
items.tips: High altitude—ascend gradually. Cold mornings even in summer; trails can be icy early season.

items.description: One of China's Four Sacred Buddhist Mountains, home to golden summits, cloud seas, ancient temples, and wild monkeys.
items.history: Buddhist activity began in the 1st century AD. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1996.
items.tips: Summit weather changes quickly; cable cars may stop in wind. Respect temple etiquette.

items.description: The world's largest stone Buddha statue carved into a cliff, overlooking the confluence of three rivers.
items.history: Carved during the Tang Dynasty (713–803 AD). Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site with Mount Emei.
items.tips: Steep stairs near the statue; queues common. Combine with a river view for classic photos.

items.description: An ancient Taoist mountain of forests, temples, and quiet paths—long regarded as a birthplace of Taoism—paired in World Heritage listing with the Dujiangyan irrigation system nearby.
items.history: Qingcheng Mountain epitomizes Taoist landscape tradition; together with Dujiangyan it forms a UNESCO World Heritage Site celebrating nature and hydraulic engineering.
items.tips: Moist climate—good footwear. Front and rear mountain routes differ in length and difficulty.

items.description: A more than 2,000-year-old irrigation system on the Min River that still regulates water for the Chengdu Plain without a large dam—ingenious divide-and-channel engineering.
items.history: Built in 256 BC during the Warring States Period. Inscribed with Mount Qingcheng as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Walk the river parks and bridges; combine with nearby Qingcheng Mountain in one trip.

items.description: A remote high-altitude scenic area with snow-capped mountains, glacial lakes, meadows, and pure nature—often called 'the last Shangri-La'.
items.history: Rose to fame through film and television. Developed as a highland eco-tourism destination in the Garzê Tibetan region.
items.tips: High altitude—watch for AMS. Weather and road conditions vary; flexible itineraries help.

items.description: Four snow-capped peaks with alpine meadows, forests, valleys, and trekking routes in the Qionglai range.
items.history: A famous mountain scenic area developed in the late 20th century.
items.tips: Mountain weather is unpredictable; permits may apply for certain routes.

items.description: One of China's best-preserved ancient cities, with traditional courtyard houses, city walls, and fengshui-aligned streets.
items.history: Founded over 2,300 years ago. A historic military and cultural city in northern Sichuan.
items.tips: Folk performances and local vinegar snacks are highlights; evenings along the river are pleasant.

items.nameCn: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
items.nameEn: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding
items.description: A conservation and research center for giant pandas, allowing visitors to see pandas up close in near-natural enclosures.
items.history: Established in 1987 to protect and breed endangered giant pandas.
items.tips: Visit early when pandas are most active. Expect crowds on holidays—book tickets online.

items.description: A low-altitude modern glacier with ice caves, waterfalls, hot springs, and views toward Gongga's snow peaks.
items.history: Developed as a glacier tourism spot in the 1980s and 1990s.
items.tips: Altitude and ice hazards on trails—follow signage. Fog can obscure peaks for days.

items.description: A vast bamboo forest covering mountains, with bamboo seas, waterfalls, caves, and bamboo culture.
items.history: Formed over centuries of bamboo cultivation. Developed as a scenic area in modern times.
items.tips: Humid and green year-round; insect repellent helps in summer.

items.description: A historic strategic pass with steep cliffs, ancient battlements, and natural terrain famed as 'the most difficult pass under heaven'.
items.history: A famous battlefield since the Three Kingdoms period. The pass has a history of over 1,700 years.
items.tips: Many steps and exposed ridges—comfortable shoes essential.

items.description: A vast Tibetan Buddhist study area with thousands of red wooden dwellings on the hills—one of the world's largest monastic communities (Larung Gar).
items.history: Founded in 1980. It has grown into one of the largest Tibetan Buddhist academies in the world.
items.tips: Altitude 3,900 m+; respect monastic rules and photography restrictions; roads may close in winter.

provinces.description: Sichuan is known as the 'Land of Abundance', famous for giant pandas, Jiuzhaigou and profound Shu culture.
provinces.history: It was the ancient Shu State. Dujiangyan is a world-famous water conservancy project. It has rich natural and cultural tourism resources.
provinces.cuisine: Mapo Tofu, Kung Pao Chicken, Twice-Cooked Pork, Dan Dan Noodles, Sichuan Hot Pot

items.description: China's largest waterfall, with a main fall and surrounding waterfalls, caves, and karst scenery.
items.history: Famous since ancient times. Developed as a national key scenic area—a symbol of Guizhou tourism.
items.tips: Rainy season swells flow; slippery decks—mind footing.

items.description: A sacred Buddhist mountain with a unique mushroom rock, steep peaks, primeval forest, and rich biodiversity.
items.history: A Buddhist site for over 1,000 years. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site in 2018.
items.tips: Weather closes upper routes sometimes; book tickets for peak periods.

items.description: The largest Miao village in China, with wooden stilt houses stacked on hillsides, night lantern views, and vibrant ethnic culture.
items.history: An ancient Miao settlement with hundreds of years of history. Developed as a major ethnic tourism site.
items.tips: Hilly terrain and crowds in peak season—light luggage helps.

items.description: An ancient riverside town with more than 2,000 years of history, featuring ancient walls, bridges, and alleys along the Wuyang River.
items.history: Built during the Qin and Han dynasties. A historic trading hub on ancient southern routes.
items.tips: Boat rides and evening river walks are popular; old streets can be slippery when wet.

items.description: A beautiful karst scenic area with clear blue water, ancient stone bridges, waterfalls, and forests—core of Libo Zhangjiang.
items.history: Part of the Libo Karst component inscribed as a UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site in 2007 (South China Karst).
items.tips: Shuttle buses cover long distances inside the park; bring rain gear.

items.description: A large Dong ethnic village with drum towers, wind-and-rain bridges, and distinctive folk customs.
items.history: An ancient Dong settlement with a long history of ethnic tradition preservation.
items.tips: Morning mist and evening lights photograph well; respect local customs during festivals.

items.description: A deep canyon with waterfalls, cliffs, karst formations, and thrilling rapids.
items.history: A natural geological landscape developed as a canyon and rafting scenic spot.
items.tips: Summer flows are strongest; check safety notices for canyon trails and water sports.

items.description: An ancient stone town with city walls, gates, courtyards, and traditional Hui and Han culture.
items.history: Built during the Ming Dynasty as a military fortress. Has a history of over 600 years.
items.tips: Weekends are busy; try rose candy and tofu dishes.

items.description: A large karst cave system with underground rivers, waterfalls, and illuminated chambers.
items.history: Developed as a cave scenic spot in the 1980s.
items.tips: Boat trips depend on water levels; wear layers inside caves.

items.description: One of China's largest and most magnificent karst caves, with spectacular stalactites and stone formations.
items.history: Discovered in the 1980s. Often called the 'king of caves' in China.
items.tips: Paths can be wet and cool; comfortable shoes and a light jacket help.

provinces.description: Guizhou is known as 'Colorful Guizhou', with rich ethnic cultures and typical karst landforms.
provinces.history: It is a multi-ethnic inhabited area with 17 native ethnic groups. It has Huangguoshu Waterfall and many ethnic villages.
provinces.cuisine: Sour Soup Fish, Huaxi Beef Noodles, Siwawa, Maotai Liquor

items.description: A well-preserved ancient Naxi town with cobblestone streets, wooden houses, canals, and traditional Dongba culture.
items.history: Built over 800 years ago. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.
items.tips: Altitude and cobblestones—comfortable shoes and slow pacing help. Respect quiet zones at night.

items.addressFull: Yulong Naxi Autonomous County, Lijiang, Yunnan, China
items.description: A snow-capped mountain with glaciers, alpine meadows, and Naxi and Tibetan cultural scenery.
items.history: Sacred to the Naxi people. Developed as a high-altitude tourist mountain in modern times.
items.bestVisitTime: November to April for snow; summer for meadows
items.tips: Altitude sickness possible—ascend gradually. Weather changes fast; check cableway status.

items.description: The historic center of the ancient Nanzhao and Dali kingdoms, with city walls, traditional buildings, and Bai ethnic culture.
items.history: Capital of the Dali Kingdom. Has a history of over 1,200 years.
items.tips: Busy commercial core—explore side alleys for calmer corners.

items.description: A highland lake surrounded by villages, fields, temples, and mountain views—core scenery of Dali.
items.history: A historic freshwater lake that has long been the life center of the Bai people.
items.tips: Ecological rules limit motor boats in some zones—follow local guidance.

items.addressFull: Shilin Yi Autonomous County, Kunming, Yunnan, China
items.description: A spectacular limestone karst stone forest with tall pillars, natural mazes, and unique geology.
items.history: Formed over 270 million years. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.
items.tips: Large site—plan routes and water. Midday sun can be intense.

items.description: A highland national park with lakes, meadows, forests, and pure plateau ecology in Shangri-La—China's first national park format in this region.
items.history: Established in 2007. Lies within the Three Parallel Rivers UNESCO World Natural Heritage landscape.
items.tips: Cold nights even in summer; shuttle buses link main sights.

items.description: China's largest tropical botanical garden with thousands of rare tropical plants.
items.history: Founded in 1959 by botanist Cai Xitao. A leading research and tourism base.
items.tips: Bring insect repellent and rain gear; tropical downpours are common.

items.description: A geothermal area with hot springs, geysers, steaming pools, and volcanic landscapes.
items.history: Used for therapeutic bathing since ancient times. Developed as a hot spring resort.
items.tips: Stay on walkways—springs are dangerously hot. Sulfur smell is normal.

items.description: A highland lake with clear water, Mosuo matrilineal culture, and island villages.
items.history: Home to the Mosuo people for centuries. Known for its unique walking marriage culture.
items.tips: Road access can be long; altitude and cold nights—dress in layers.

items.description: A sacred snow-capped range with magnificent peaks and famous 'golden summit' sunrise views—especially over Kawagarbo.
items.history: Sacred to Tibetans. Climbing is restricted; it is a major photography and pilgrimage site.
items.bestVisitTime: October to May for clearer skies
items.tips: Clear peaks are rare—plan flexible days. Respect local cultural sites.

items.description: A remote village at the foot of Meili Snow Mountain, reachable mainly on foot, with pristine scenery.
items.history: A traditional Tibetan village isolated from the outside world for a long time.
items.tips: Trekking requires fitness and guides on some routes; weather can close paths.

items.description: Magnificent terraced rice fields carved into mountains by the Hani people over millennia.
items.history: Built over 1,300 years. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Cultural Landscape Heritage in 2013.
items.tips: Winter–spring water mirrors; arrive before dawn for classic shots. Respect fields and farmers.

items.description: A quieter ancient Naxi town near Lijiang, preserving traditional architecture, canals, and lifestyle.
items.history: An ancient market town with a history of over 800 years. Less commercial than the main Lijiang Old Town.
items.tips: Morning light is best for photos; combine ticket with Lijiang if bundled; altitude ~2,400 m.

provinces.description: Yunnan is known as 'South of the Colorful Clouds', a kingdom of animals and plants with 25 ethnic minorities.
provinces.history: It was the ancient Dian Kingdom. It has rich biodiversity and colorful ethnic customs, known as a world-famous tourist resort.
provinces.cuisine: Cross-Bridge Rice Noodles, Steam Pot Chicken, Xuanwei Ham, Pu'er Tea, Flower Cake

items.description: An iconic hilltop palace complex in Lhasa with Tibetan architecture, golden roofs, ancient murals, precious Buddhist relics, and tombs of past Dalai Lamas—the symbol of Tibet.
items.history: Built in the 7th century under King Songtsen Gampo and expanded in the 17th century. It served as the winter residence of the Dalai Lamas and the political-religious center of Tibet. Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1994.
items.tips: Timed tickets and ID checks are strict; no photography in some halls.

items.description: A revered Buddhist temple in central Lhasa housing the Jowo Shakyamuni statue, surrounded by pilgrims, prayer wheels, and Tibetan artwork.
items.history: Founded in the 7th century during the Tang Dynasty. It is the spiritual heart of Tibetan Buddhism and part of the Potala Palace UNESCO ensemble.
items.tips: Crowded at prayer times; follow photography rules and clockwise circulation.

items.description: A circular ancient street in Lhasa lined with handicraft shops, prayer flags, and pilgrims—combining religious practice, local life, and commerce.
items.history: Formed around Jokhang Temple over centuries as a pilgrimage and trading route.
items.tips: Watch belongings in crowds; haggle politely for souvenirs.

items.description: One of China's largest saltwater lakes, set among snow-capped Nyenchen Tanglha peaks—vast blue waters, grassy shorelines, and nomadic tents.
items.history: Formed by tectonic movements in the Himalayan orogeny. Regarded as a holy lake in Tibetan Buddhism.
items.tips: Very high altitude—rest in Lhasa first. Roads may close in winter snow.

items.description: A stunning turquoise lake winding through mountain valleys—vivid color and peaceful scenery, classic view from Kamba La Pass.
items.history: A tectonic lake millions of years old, revered as one of Tibet's three sacred lakes.
items.tips: Altitude and glare—sunglasses and layers. Weather changes quickly on the pass.

items.description: A spectacular natural canyon with extreme elevation drops, dense forests, waterfalls, and rare wildlife—among the world's deepest river gorges.
items.history: Formed by the Yarlung Zangbo River cutting through the Himalayas, with unique geological evolution.
items.tips: Monsoon clouds often hide peaks; check local access and permits for remote sections.

items.description: A high-altitude camp on Everest's north side offering views of the world's highest summit and mountaineering culture.
items.history: Located on the northern slope of Qomolangma; supports expeditions and regulated high-altitude tourism.
items.tips: Extreme altitude; travel requires permits and acclimatization. Weather often obscures the summit.

items.description: A large monastery in Shigatse with grand halls, golden stupas, giant Buddha statues, and Tibetan Buddhist art—the traditional seat of the Panchen Lama.
items.history: Founded in 1447 by the first Dalai Lama. It has long been a major Gelugpa monastery.
items.tips: Respect photography bans indoors; afternoons can be less crowded.

items.description: A distinctive snow-capped pyramidal peak sacred in Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and Bon—pilgrims perform kora around it.
items.history: For thousands of years a key pilgrimage site where religious myths cross South Asian cultures.
items.tips: High altitude and remote logistics—plan guides and permits. Respect sacred landscape rules.

items.description: A highland freshwater lake near Mount Kailash with crystal-clear waters—a central site for pilgrimage and tranquil scenery.
items.history: Formed by Himalayan glaciation; revered as a sacred lake paired with Mount Kailash.
items.tips: Wind and cold even in summer; altitude sickness is common—ascend gradually.

items.description: Ancient castle and cave ruins on a red cliff in Ngari, with murals, temples, and residential remains from the former Guge Kingdom.
items.history: Established in the 10th century; the kingdom flourished for over 700 years before its decline, preserving western Tibetan art and culture.
items.tips: Remote drive from Shigatse; bring supplies and check travel permits.

provinces.description: Tibet is located on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, known as the 'Roof of the World', with unique Tibetan culture and religious heritage.
provinces.history: Tibet has been an inalienable part of China's territory since ancient times. It has the Potala Palace and world-famous plateau scenery.
provinces.cuisine: Butter Tea, Tsampa, Barley Wine, Yak Meat, Air-Dried Meat

items.nameEn: Terracotta Army (Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor)
items.description: An archaeological wonder with thousands of life-sized terracotta warriors and horses reflecting the military might of the Qin Empire—a symbol of ancient Chinese civilization.
items.history: Built in the Qin Dynasty (221–207 BCE) as the mausoleum of China's first emperor. Discovered in 1974; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.
items.tips: Book timed-entry tickets early; peak holidays are very crowded. Allow half a day including museums.

items.description: A steep granite mountain with five main peaks, narrow plank roads, and Taoist temples—famous for thrilling hiking and cliff views.
items.history: Formed over 120 million years by tectonic uplift and erosion. A sacred Taoist mountain with religious construction spanning dynasties.
items.tips: Check weather; some paths close in wind or ice. Start early; cable cars reduce hiking time.

items.description: A massive rectangular fortification encircling central Xi'an, with watchtowers and ramparts—visitors can cycle atop the wall for panoramic views.
items.history: Constructed during the early Ming Dynasty (1370–1378) on Tang Dynasty foundations. One of the best-preserved ancient city walls in China.
items.tips: Cycling on the wall is popular; sunset views are excellent. Mind summer heat.

items.description: The Giant Wild Goose Pagoda is a Tang Buddhist landmark built to store scriptures from India; nearby Tang Paradise is a modern cultural park with gardens and performances evoking Chang'an at its height.
items.history: The pagoda was built in 652 CE during the Tang Dynasty to house Buddhist scriptures brought from India.
items.tips: Combine with Da Ci'en Temple area; evening fountain shows nearby on schedule.

items.addressFull: Qujiang New District, Xi'an, Shaanxi, China
items.description: A large Tang-themed cultural park near the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda, with classical gardens, performances, and architecture inspired by Chang'an's imperial prosperity.
items.history: Developed as a modern scenic park beside Qujiang Pool to showcase Tang Dynasty culture, festivals, and night lighting.
items.tips: Night lighting and shows draw crowds—check official schedules.

items.description: A revered Buddhist temple with an underground palace holding Buddha's finger relics and treasures—combining ancient architecture with a modern museum of Buddhist art.
items.history: Established in the Eastern Han Dynasty; expanded in the Tang as a royal Buddhist temple famous for the finger relics.
items.tips: The site is large—wear comfortable shoes; allow several hours.

items.description: A collection of revolutionary memorials, former leaders' residences, and exhibition halls preserving the history of the Chinese revolution in the 1930s–1940s.
items.history: Yan'an was a core base of the Chinese revolution; sites include Zaoyuan, Yangjialing, and command centers.
items.tips: Several sites are spread across the city—plan transport between locations.

items.addressFull: Yichuan County, Yan'an, Shaanxi, China (shared with Shanxi)
items.description: The second-largest waterfall in China, where the Yellow River roars through a narrow gorge on the Loess Plateau—powerful currents and mist.
items.history: Formed by the Yellow River cutting through the plateau over millennia; celebrated in classical texts.
items.tips: Water volume varies by season; mist and spray are heavy—protect cameras.

items.nameEn: Mausoleum of the Yellow Emperor (Xuanyuan Temple)
items.description: A solemn memorial complex with ancient cypresses, halls, and steles dedicated to the legendary Yellow Emperor—host to grand ancestor-worship ceremonies.
items.history: Sacrificial traditions honoring Huangdi as a cultural ancestor date back thousands of years.
items.tips: Qingming festival draws pilgrims; weekdays are quieter.

items.description: The highest peak of the Qinling range, with vertical vegetation zones, alpine lakes, and snow—known for cool summers and biodiversity.
items.history: A historic Taoist retreat and nature reserve; long valued for ecology and scenery.
items.tips: Altitude and weather change quickly; check park buses and trail openings.

items.description: A grand Tang imperial mausoleum carved into a mountain for Emperor Gaozong and Wu Zetian, with spirit paths and stone figures.
items.history: Built in the Tang Dynasty as the joint tomb of Gaozong and Wu Zetian—China's only ruling empress in name—preserving exceptional stone sculpture.
items.tips: Combine with nearby satellite tombs if time allows; uneven ground on hills.

provinces.description: Shaanxi is known as 'Land of Three Qins'. Xi'an is an ancient capital with 13 dynasties establishing capitals here.
provinces.history: It is the birthplace of Chinese civilization. It has Terracotta Army, Huashan Mountain and other world-famous historical heritages.
provinces.cuisine: Roujiamo, Yangrou Paomo, Liangpi, Saozi Noodles, Youpo Noodles

items.description: A vast complex of caves with exquisite murals, painted sculptures, and ancient manuscripts—a masterpiece of Buddhist art along the Silk Road.
items.history: Carved from the 4th to 14th centuries. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.
items.tips: Tickets are limited and timed—book well ahead. Photography rules are strict inside caves.

items.description: Singing sand dunes surrounding a small crescent-shaped spring in the desert—combining desert adventure with an oasis landmark.
items.history: Formed by desert wind and landform evolution; recorded as a scenic spot since the Han Dynasty.
items.tips: Sand gets hot midday; sunrise/sunset are best. Protect electronics from sand.

items.description: A well-preserved Ming Dynasty fort at the western end of the Great Wall—strategic Silk Road fortress with walls, towers, and gates.
items.history: Built in the Ming Dynasty as the western terminus of the Great Wall frontier defense.
items.tips: Windy and dry—carry water and layers. Museum and wall walks take a few hours.

items.description: Striking layered red, orange, and yellow rock formations—often called 'rainbow mountains'—a famous geological and photography destination.
items.history: Formed over 24 million years by sedimentation and erosion; celebrated globally for its colorful Danxia landforms.
items.tips: Best light near sunrise/sunset; stay on boardwalks to protect fragile formations.

items.description: Thousands of Buddhist statues carved into a red sandstone cliff—often called the 'Oriental Sculpture Museum'.
items.history: Carved from the 4th century onward along a freestanding cliff in Tianshui.
items.tips: Steep walkways and stairs; not ideal for severe vertigo. Busy on holidays.

items.description: Ancient cave statues and murals in a Yellow River canyon—early Buddhist art spread along inland river routes.
items.history: Carving began in the Western Jin Dynasty along the Yellow River in Linxia.
items.tips: Access often involves reservoir boat trips—check water levels and schedules.

items.description: A secluded Tibetan stone village surrounded by steep peaks and forests—Tibetan culture, pastoral scenery, and rugged terrain.
items.history: Traditional Tibetan hamlets and landforms shaped by alpine geology; long a cultural landscape of eastern Tibet.
items.tips: Roads can be rough; altitude and weather change quickly. Respect local customs.

items.description: A sprawling Gelugpa monastery with golden roofs, prayer halls, and a major Buddhist college—host to grand festivals.
items.history: Founded in 1709; one of the largest Gelugpa monasteries outside the Tibet Autonomous Region.
items.tips: Dress modestly; follow monastery rules for photos and circuits.

items.description: Lush forests, clear lakes, cascading waterfalls, and karst scenery—a quiet natural resort in southern Gansu.
items.history: An alpine forest and canyon zone developed for eco-tourism and hiking.
items.tips: Shuttle buses cover part of the route; trails can be slippery after rain.

items.description: Ruins of an ancient frontier pass in the Gobi, with beacon towers and exhibits on Silk Road travel beyond Dunhuang.
items.history: A Han Dynasty strategic pass on the Silk Road used for border defense and trade control.
items.tips: Desert heat and wind—bring sun protection. Combine with Jade Gate Pass if touring.

items.description: Ancient desert pass ruins marking the historical frontier—famous from classical poetry and Silk Road journeys.
items.history: Built in the Han Dynasty as a key western pass; often paired with Yang Pass in Dunhuang tours.
items.tips: Open desert—sun and wind protection; often combined with Yardang or Mogao day tours by car.

provinces.description: Gansu is a key section of the ancient Silk Road, known as the 'Hexi Corridor', a hub of cultural exchange between East and West.
provinces.history: It has a long history of the Silk Road. It has Mogao Caves, Jiayuguan Pass and other world-famous historical sites.
provinces.cuisine: Lanzhou Beef Noodles, Hand-Torn Mutton, Niangpi

items.description: A vast blue lake surrounded by grasslands, mountains, and Tibetan villages—famous for bird islands and highland scenery.
items.history: Formed by tectonic depression; China's largest inland saltwater lake, supporting nomadic life and religious traditions for ages.
items.tips: Altitude ~3200 m—pace yourself. Weather shifts quickly; ring road trips need fuel planning.

items.description: A wide salt flat with reflective white surfaces—popularly called the 'Mirror of the Sky' for photography.
items.history: A salt lake from ancient seawater retreat; mined for salt for centuries.
items.tips: Bright sun and salt—sunglasses and shoe covers help. Wind reduces mirror effect.

items.description: A large monastery with golden roofs, butter sculptures, murals, and appliqué art—the birthplace of Tsongkhapa in tradition.
items.history: Founded in the 16th century; one of the most important Gelugpa monasteries outside Lhasa, hosting the Great Prayer Festival.
items.tips: No photos in many halls; hire a guide for context. Busy during Tibetan festivals.

items.description: A vast uninhabited plateau grassland and wetland—home to Tibetan antelopes and other rare wildlife under strict protection.
items.history: A remote highland wilderness on the Tibetan Plateau; UNESCO World Heritage natural site for biodiversity.
items.tips: UNESCO natural site—travel with permits and guides; no casual off-roading.

items.description: Expansive golden rape flower fields in summer, backed by snow mountains—a spectacular seasonal agricultural sight.
items.history: A highland agricultural landscape of barley and rape cultivation along the Qilian foothills.
items.tips: Peak bloom is short—check local reports. High UV at altitude.

items.description: Red rock peaks with grassy slopes overlooking the Qilian range—panoramic views of snow mountains and forested valleys.
items.history: A Danxia-style viewpoint in Qilian County, prized for sunrise and alpine vistas.
items.tips: Wooden walkways; afternoon storms possible. Altitude ~3000 m.

items.description: China's largest salt lake by area—huge salt flats, industrial brine ponds, and striking saline scenery.
items.history: Formed by long-term salt accumulation in the Qaidam Basin; major salt production base.
items.tips: Industrial area—follow visitor rules; salt crust can be sharp.

items.description: A vividly turquoise lake in the Qaidam Basin—contrasting blue-green water with the surrounding Gobi.
items.history: A tectonic salt lake with high mineral content in eastern Qaidam.
items.tips: Remote—fuel and supplies needed; access rules change—verify locally.

items.description: Pristine alpine lakes, snow peaks, and grasslands in a sacred mountain region of eastern Tibet—strict access policies may apply.
items.history: A highland lake group revered in Tibetan Buddhism; ecology and culture are tightly protected.
items.tips: Check latest park access policies before travel; altitude and weather are serious.

items.description: A folk culture park showcasing Tu architecture, costumes, rituals, and traditional rural life.
items.history: Preserves Tu ethnic customs in Huzhu with historic village forms and festivals.
items.tips: Festival dates add crowds; respect local customs during rituals.

provinces.description: Qinghai is the source of the Yangtze, Yellow and Lancang rivers, known as 'China's Water Tower' and 'Source of Three Rivers'.
provinces.history: It has the largest inland saltwater lake Qinghai Lake and unique plateau scenery. It is a multi-ethnic inhabited area on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.
provinces.cuisine: Hand-Torn Mutton, Yogurt, Tsampa, Barley Wine

items.description: Where the Tengger Desert meets the Yellow River—sand sliding, camel riding, Yellow River rafting, and desert control showcases.
items.history: A desert landscape at the southern bend of the Yellow River, developed for tourism and sand-control projects.
items.tips: Sand and sun protection essential; book activities in busy seasons.

items.description: A rustic film set with desert-style architecture—famous for classic Chinese frontier and martial-arts films.
items.history: Built on ancient frontier castle ruins; now a cultural theme park for visitors.
items.tips: Exposed site—midday heat is intense; morning or late afternoon better.

items.description: Pyramid-like royal tombs on the plain—remains of the Western Xia dynasty, often called the 'Eastern Pyramids'.
items.history: Built during the Western Xia Dynasty (11th–13th centuries); preserves the lost culture of the Tangut realm.
items.tips: Museum first for context; windy open terrain—layers help.

items.description: A lake surrounded by reeds and sand dunes—birds, fish, and a blend of desert and wetland scenery.
items.history: A wetland formed by natural water accumulation where desert meets lake.
items.tips: Bird migration seasons are best for wildlife; weekends busy.

items.description: Ancient petroglyphs on Helan Mountain cliffs—hunting scenes and nomadic life from prehistory to Western Xia.
items.history: Created by ancient nomadic peoples; a major rock-art gallery of northern China.
items.tips: Rocky paths; interpretive signs help. Combine with nearby wineries if interested.

items.description: A forested highland associated with the Long March—green mountains, trails, and revolutionary memorials.
items.history: Historic mountain landscape in southern Ningxia combining nature and red-tourism sites.
items.tips: Cooler than lowlands—bring jacket. Roads can be winding.

items.description: Cliffside Buddhist caves and statues from the Northern Wei onward—fine sculpture along the Silk Road fringe.
items.history: Carved from the Northern Wei Dynasty; reflects Buddhism's spread in the northwest.
items.tips: Steep steps between niches; allow 2–3 hours.

items.description: Prehistoric Paleolithic site with stone tools, ancient settlements, and canyon landforms—among China's early excavated human sites.
items.history: Documents early human activity on the edge of the Ordos and Yellow River.
items.tips: Mixed indoor/outdoor—wind in spring. Shuttle links distant sections.

provinces.description: Ningxia is China's only Hui autonomous region, known as 'Jiangnan Beyond the Great Wall', rich in wolfberry resources.
provinces.history: It has a long history of ethnic integration. It has Western Xia Imperial Tombs and unique desert and oasis scenery.
provinces.cuisine: Hand-Torn Mutton, Mutton Saozi Noodles, Eight-Treasure Tea, Goji Berries

items.description: A turquoise alpine lake in the Altai, surrounded by forests and snow peaks—colorful autumn forests and Tuvan pastoral culture.
items.history: A glacial lake in the Altai with long-standing nomadic Tuvan communities.
items.tips: Park buses required; book lodging in peak season. Cold nights even in summer.

items.description: A deep blue glacial lake beneath Bogda Peak—framed by Tianshan spruce forests and classic northwest scenery.
items.history: On the north slope of Bogda; regarded as a sacred site in local traditions.
items.tips: Altitude and crowds on holidays—arrive early. Weather changes fast.

items.description: Vast green meadows on rolling hills—yurts, livestock, and Kazakh nomadic culture; known as the 'Sky Grassland'.
items.history: A mountain grassland formed by favorable alpine climate; home to Kazakh herders.
items.tips: Peak season prices rise; book yurts ahead. Respect pasture fencing.

items.description: A clear blue highland lake ringed by snow mountains and grasslands—the 'Pearl of the Tianshan'.
items.history: A tectonic lake formed by mountain movements along the northern Silk Road routes.
items.tips: Very windy; circle road is long—plan fuel and time. Cold at night.

items.description: A maze of ancient streets, wooden houses, bazaars, and mosques—two millennia of Silk Road trade and Uygur life.
items.history: A historic trading hub on the Silk Road for over two thousand years.
items.tips: Respect local customs; morning markets are lively. Dry climate—hydrate.

items.description: A wooden village of the Tuva people beside forests and rivers—famous for golden autumn and quiet rural life.
items.history: A traditional village in the Altai maintaining pastoral ways of life.
items.tips: Remote with park transfers; winter access is limited. Book lodging early.

items.description: Red sandstone hills with extreme summer heat—famous from Journey to the West and desert vistas.
items.history: Formed by uplift and erosion; iconic Turpan landform.
items.bestVisitTime: April to June; September to October
items.tips: Avoid midday heat in July–August; carry water. Quick stops along the road.

items.description: A lush oasis valley with grape trellises, fruit gardens, and Uygur courtyard houses in the Turpan basin.
items.history: A thousand-year history of grapes and karez irrigation in the desert.
items.tips: Grape harvest season is busiest; try local raisins and juices.

items.description: Vast flat grasslands with winding rivers, swan habitat, and Kazakh yurt culture—China's second-largest grassland.
items.history: Highland wetland prairie famous for migratory swans and open horizons.
items.tips: Cold and windy—bring layers. Mosquitoes near water in summer.

items.description: Remote highland with snow peaks, stone villages, and Tajik culture at the edge of the Pamir—the 'Roof of the World'.
items.history: Formed by Himalayan orogeny; historic cross-border plateau routes.
items.tips: Border permits required for some routes; altitude sickness risk—ascend gradually.

items.description: A steep, winding mountain road with dramatic valley views—showcasing highland road engineering on an ancient transport route.
items.history: Evolved from historic mountain paths; now a famous scenic drive near Tashkurgan.
items.tips: Check road conditions and permits; not for those prone to motion sickness.

items.description: A narrow red-rock canyon with towering cliffs—striking erosion landforms in the ancient Qiuci region.
items.history: Formed by erosion in red sandstone; major Kuqa geological sight.
items.tips: Avoid entering during rain (flash floods); sturdy shoes for wet rocky floors.

items.addressFull: G217 through Tianshan from Dushanzi to Kuqa, Xinjiang, China
items.description: A legendary highway crossing the Tianshan—forests, snow passes, and desert in one journey among China's most scenic roads.
items.history: Built as a strategic mountain highway (G217) linking north and south Xinjiang; seasonal opening only.
items.tips: Closed or risky in winter; check snow/landslide closures; fuel and supplies between long empty sections; altitude and weather change fast.

provinces.description: Xinjiang is China's largest provincial-level administrative region, known as 'Land of Fruits' and 'Land of Song and Dance'.
provinces.history: Xinjiang has been an inalienable part of China's territory since ancient times. It is an important section of the ancient Silk Road.
provinces.cuisine: Big Plate Chicken, Pilaf, Lamb Kebabs, Naan, Lagman

items.description: A famous natural harbor between Hong Kong Island and Kowloon—skyline views, nightly light shows, and busy marine traffic.
items.history: Formed by post-glacial sea-level rise; developed into a global trade hub under British administration and after reunification.
items.tips: Sunset and evening are popular for photography. Check ferry and cruise schedules on site.

items.description: A theme park with classic Disney rides, parades, castles, and attractions adapted for Asian visitors.
items.history: Opened in 2005 as the fifth Disneyland resort worldwide, blending Disney stories with Chinese cultural elements.
items.tips: Check park hours and ticket/reservation policies in advance. Weekends and holidays may require extra wait time.

items.description: The highest point on Hong Kong Island—historic Peak Tram and sweeping views of the harbor and city.
items.history: A historic sightseeing spot since the colonial era.
items.tips: Go early for clearer views. Evening visits are popular but can be crowded—plan extra time.

items.addressFull: Hong Kong Island, Wong Chuk Hang
items.description: A large park with ocean exhibits, thrill rides, pandas, and conservation education—opened in 1977.
items.history: Opened in 1977 as a marine and animal theme park combining entertainment and conservation.
items.tips: Check opening hours and ticket policies. Arrive early to avoid peak queues on popular rides.

items.description: A waterfront shopping and museum district facing Victoria Harbour—boutiques, cultural venues, and harbor views.
items.history: Developed since the late 19th century as a commercial and tourism hub on the Kowloon shore.
items.tips: Evening is popular for skyline photography. Expect crowds on weekends—arrive earlier for a more relaxed walk.

items.description: A busy shopping and dining district with skyscrapers, department stores, and urban energy.
items.history: Evolved from early urban development into a major luxury retail center.
items.tips: Late afternoons and evenings are lively. Use public transit when possible and plan for crowds in peak shopping seasons.

items.description: Hong Kong's central business district—skyscrapers, banks, government buildings, and luxury retail at the colonial heart of the city.
items.history: The historic business and administrative core since British times.
items.tips: Weekdays can be crowded during commuting hours. Comfortable shoes recommended for walking between areas.

items.description: A dense commercial district with street markets, small shops, food stalls, and intense local energy.
items.history: Known for street markets and local culture amid high population density.
items.tips: Evenings can be busy—keep an eye on personal belongings and allow extra time for walking through crowds.

items.description: A colorful Taoist temple popular for fortune-telling and prayers—early 20th-century architecture.
items.history: Built in the early 20th century; one of Hong Kong's busiest places of worship.
items.tips: Dress respectfully and follow on-site guidance. Weekends and festivals can be busy.

items.addressFull: West Kowloon Cultural District, Hong Kong
items.description: A modern museum in West Kowloon displaying Palace Museum collections and imperial Chinese art.
items.history: Opened in 2022 to exhibit masterpieces on long-term loan from Beijing's Palace Museum.
items.tips: Check exhibition schedules and ticketing requirements in advance. Weekends can be busy—arrive earlier if possible.

items.addressFull: Ngong Ping, Lantau Island, Hong Kong
items.description: The world's tallest outdoor seated bronze Buddha, located on the summit of Muyu Peak, Ngong Ping, Lantau Island, Hong Kong. Sitting atop a 3-tiered altar modeled after the Temple of Heaven in Beijing, it faces north, overlooking the city. It is a major religious and tourist landmark, combining solemn Buddhist art with impressive modern engineering.
items.history: Initiated by the Po Lin Monastery in 1973, the project was formally launched in 1981. Constructed by China Aerospace Science and Industry's Nanjing Chenguang Machinery Plant, it was completed in 1989 and consecrated on December 29, 1993. Standing 34 meters high and weighing 250 tons, it took 12 years and over HK$60 million to build, representing a significant achievement in modern Buddhist statue art.
items.tips: Ngong Ping 360 cable car can queue heavily—book or go early; mist may obscure views; modest dress at monastery.

provinces.description: Hong Kong is an international financial, trade and shipping center, known as the 'Pearl of the Orient'.
provinces.history: Hong Kong is a special administrative region of China. It returned to China in 1997. It is an inalienable part of China's territory.
provinces.cuisine: Hong Kong-style Milk Tea, Egg Tarts, Wonton Noodles, Roasted Meats

items.description: An iconic stone facade of a 17th-century church—symbol of Macao's blend of Chinese and European heritage.
items.history: Built in the 17th century as part of St. Paul's College; the facade survived a fire in 1835. UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Visit earlier in the day for lighter crowds. Nearby streets can be busy—keep valuables secure.

items.description: Historic streets, churches, temples, and squares blending European and Chinese architecture in the old town core.
items.history: Formed over centuries of Sino-Portuguese exchange. UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.tips: Plan a walking route and wear comfortable shoes. Some sites may have separate opening hours and ticket rules.

items.description: A tall tower with panoramic views, bungee jumping, restaurants, and cultural events—opened in 2001.
