items.history: Opened in 2001 for observation and adventure tourism.
items.tips: Go near sunset for changing light. Check ticketing and opening hours in advance.

items.description: A historic lane on Taipa with small shops, food stalls, temples, and Portuguese-influenced streets.
items.history: Traditional southern Chinese village fabric mixed with colonial-era buildings.
items.tips: Evenings can be crowded—go earlier for a more relaxed visit. Keep an eye on personal belongings.

items.description: A luxury resort with indoor canals, gondola rides, shopping malls, and entertainment—opened in 2007.
items.history: Opened in 2007, modeled after Venice, Italy.
items.tips: Great option in hot or rainy weather. Check event schedules if you want shows or exhibitions.

items.description: A paved European-style square with fountains—historic civic heart of Macao's old town.
items.history: A public square since colonial times, surrounded by pastel neoclassical facades.
items.tips: Comfortable shoes recommended. Many nearby heritage sites have their own opening hours.

items.description: One of Macao's oldest temples, dedicated to the sea goddess Mazu—traditional pavilions above the harbor.
items.history: Built in the 15th century; reflects Macao's maritime roots.
items.tips: Dress respectfully and follow on-site guidance. Photography rules may vary in certain areas.

items.description: A spacious black-sand beach on Coloane with coastal trails and open sea views.
items.history: Natural black sand beach—Macao's largest seaside recreation area.
items.tips: Check weather and sea conditions. Sun protection recommended, especially in summer.

provinces.description: Macau is an international tourism and leisure center, a historic city integrating Chinese and Western cultures.
provinces.history: Macau is a special administrative region of China. It returned to China in 1999. It is an inalienable part of China's territory.
provinces.cuisine: Portuguese Egg Tarts, Pork Chop Bun, Portuguese Chicken, Almond Cookies

items.description: Taiwan's largest alpine lake, with sun-shaped and moon-shaped water areas—surrounded by mountains and indigenous villages.
items.history: A tectonic lake and historic scenic area of central Taiwan.
items.tips: Consider a lakeside bike ride and a short cruise. Morning light is often best for calm views.

items.description: High mountain forests, sunrise views, forest railway, and sea of clouds—classic central Taiwan alpine scenery.
items.history: Developed from timber and tourism industries; famous for sunrise over the cloud sea.
items.tips: Bring layers for cooler mountain weather. Start early for sunrise viewpoints when conditions allow.

items.description: A world-famous museum of Chinese imperial art, ceramics, jade, and calligraphy—collections rooted in the Forbidden City treasures.
items.history: Founded in 1925; houses masterpieces carried to Taiwan from the former Palace collections.
items.tips: Check ticketing and current exhibitions in advance. Allow extra time on weekends and holidays.

items.description: Taiwan's first national park—tropical beaches, coral reefs, forests, and rich coastal ecology in the far south.
items.history: Established in 1982 as Taiwan's first national park.
items.tips: Sun protection is essential. Check weather and sea conditions, especially during typhoon season.

items.description: A coastal geopark with mushroom rocks, honeycomb weathering, and tidal pools—classic northern shore geology.
items.history: Formed by coastal erosion into distinctive hoodoo and sea-cave landforms.
items.tips: Coastal winds can be strong—bring a light jacket. Follow marked paths to protect fragile formations.

items.description: A deep marble canyon with sheer cliffs, turquoise rivers, and hiking trails through one of the world's great gorge landscapes.
items.history: Protected as a national park; carved by the Liwu River through marble bedrock.
items.tips: Check trail conditions and weather alerts. Some routes may require permits or close during heavy rain.

items.description: A super-tall skyscraper with observation decks and malls—completed in 2004 as an engineering icon.
items.history: Completed in 2004; long ranked among the world's tallest buildings.
items.tips: Visit near sunset for changing light. Tickets for observation decks may sell out during peak times.

items.description: Hillside alleys with teahouses, snacks, and nostalgic Japanese-era architecture—former gold-mining townscape.
items.history: Developed from gold-rush days into a cultural tourism village.
items.tips: Rain is common—bring a light rain jacket. Evenings are atmospheric but can be crowded.

items.description: Steep marble cliffs dropping to the Pacific—dramatic coastal scenery along the Suhua Highway.
items.history: Part of the Central Mountain Range meeting the ocean—rapid uplift and erosion.
items.tips: Watch for strong wind and sun exposure. Viewpoints can be along roads—follow safety signs carefully.

items.description: A volcanic island archipelago with basalt columns, beaches, fishing villages, and maritime culture.
items.history: Long history of fishing and trading across the Taiwan Strait.
items.tips: Ferry and flight schedules vary by season—book ahead. Bring sun protection and check wind conditions.

provinces.description: Taiwan is China's largest island, known as 'Treasure Island', with rich natural scenery and cultural heritage.
provinces.history: Taiwan has been an inalienable part of China's territory since ancient times. It has Sun Moon Lake, Ali Mountain and other famous scenic spots.
provinces.cuisine: Oyster Omelet, Bubble Tea, Braised Pork Rice, Pineapple Cake, Sun Cake
